verse.zh: 可见信道是从听道来的，听道是从基督的话来的<small>罗马书 10:17</small>
verse.en: So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.<small>Romans 10:17</small>

verseText.zh: 可见信道是从听道来的，听道是从基督的话来的
verseText.en: So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.

summary.zh: 从“信心是对上帝的确信”讲起：信心包含对上帝话语的信心，让上帝的话语引导我们，而不是用感受来定义上帝；认识“信道是从听道来的”（罗马书10:17）与原文词义——pistis（信心）、akoe（听道）、rhema（当下上帝正在说的话）；分享在生活中经历上帝话语的四种方式、话语的查验与马利亚的榜样；辨析rhema与logos——神的话语都有能力，关键在领受、接受与顺服；再讲如何查验领受——与圣经相背离的确信不是信心，期待也不是信心；最后讲“理性认知、情感盼望、意志顺服”三者合一的全人全心的信心。附2个思考问题。
summary.en: Faith is confidence in God. Starting from “faith comes from hearing” (Romans 10:17), this sermon unpacks the Greek words—pistis (faith), akoe (hearing), and rhema (the word God is speaking now)—and shares four ways to encounter God’s word in daily life, how to test what you receive, and Mary’s example of treasuring God’s revelation. It contrasts rhema and logos, showing that every word of God carries power; what matters is receiving, accepting, and obeying. It then teaches how to test what you receive—convictions that contradict the Bible are not faith, and expectation is not faith either. Finally, it presents whole-hearted faith as the union of rational understanding, emotional hope, and willing obedience. With 2 reflection questions.

blocks.zh: 信心简单地说是我们对事物的确信，而基督徒从神而来的信心是确信什么呢？基督徒的信心是对上帝的确信！对上帝的信心也包含对上帝话语的信心！因为上帝的话语是我们认识的上帝的最终标准。
blocks.en: Faith, simply put, is our confidence in something. For a Christian, faith from God is confidence in what? The Christian’s faith is confidence in God! Faith in God also includes faith in God’s word, for God’s word is the final standard by which we know God.

blocks.zh: 我们的感受和经历会验证上帝话语是真实的；但我们的感受不能代替或者否认上帝的话语。因为人的感受是个人主观上感知，每个人对相同事物的感受不一样。并且在不同时间段，每个个体的感受也会发生变化。让上帝的话语来引导你，不要用自己的感受来定义上帝。
blocks.en: Our feelings and experiences can confirm that God’s word is true; but our feelings can never replace or deny God’s word. Human feelings are subjective perceptions—different people feel differently about the same thing, and each person’s feelings change over time. Let God’s word guide you; do not define God by your feelings.

blocks.zh: 如果上帝是唯一的真理，就不是你的实践可以去检验其是不是真理；而是让祂的话语去纠正你的行为。人的传统和神学可能会出错，可以用你对上帝话语的认知和你的经历去验证，但上帝的话语永远可以引导我们的生活。所以，圣经经历了几千年人类社会的发展，依然是这个世界最畅销的书籍。
blocks.en: If God is the only truth, then it is not your practice that tests whether He is truth; rather, His word corrects your behavior. Human traditions and theology can err—you may verify them against your knowledge of God’s word and your experience—but God’s word can always guide our lives. That is why the Bible, after thousands of years of human history, remains the world’s best-selling book.

title.zh: 一、信心的源头：上帝的话语
title.en: I. The source of faith: God’s word

blocks.zh: 信心的源头是上帝，而上帝使用祂的话语——圣经经文，来锚定我们的信心。
blocks.en: The source of faith is God, and God uses His word—the Scriptures—to anchor our faith.

blocks.zh: “信道”的原文的发音是“pistis {pis'-tis}匹斯替丝”。是对真理或者对上帝的坚信和忠贞，你也可以简单地来说是“信心”。也就是说，信心是从听道来的。这里的“听道”原文发音是“akoe {ak-o-ay'}艾口”。对上帝的信心和忠贞是听见了一些事。所以基督徒要想对上帝能够火热起来，你需要听啊。听什么呢？基督的话。“话”的发音是“rhema {hray'-mah}”，强调说的动作。
blocks.en: The Greek behind "faith" is pronounced "pistis"—firm belief in and loyalty to the truth, or to God. In short, it is "faith." That is, faith comes from hearing. The word "hearing" is pronounced "akoe." Faith in and loyalty to God come from hearing certain things. So if a Christian wants to grow fervent for God, you need to hear. Hear what? The word of Christ. The Greek word here for "word" is "rhema," emphasizing the action of speaking.

blocks.zh: 这个概念最早由古希腊哲学家柏拉图提出，他将词汇分为“onoma”（名词）和“rhema”（动词）。后来亚里士多德及布拉格学派进一步发展了这一思想，使其成为现代语言学理论的基础之一。
blocks.en: This concept was first proposed by the ancient Greek philosopher Plato, who divided words into "onoma" (nouns) and "rhema" (verbs). Aristotle and later the Prague School developed this idea further, making it one of the foundations of modern linguistics.

blocks.zh: 综合来看，我们的信心是因为听见基督对我们生命的说话。我们怎么理解基督对我们说话呢？狭义的理解就是基督在你面前说话，但从圣经的角度来看，不仅仅是和基督面对面，因为基督已经在天父的右边为我们代求。
blocks.en: Taken together, our faith comes from hearing Christ speak into our lives. How do we understand Christ speaking to us? In a narrow sense, Christ speaks to you face to face; but from a biblical perspective it is not only face to face, because Christ is now interceding for us at the right hand of the Father.

zh.label: 圣经 · 罗马书 10:17
zh.text: 可见信道是从听道来的，听道是从基督的话来的。

en.label: Scripture · Romans 10:17
en.text: So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.

title.zh: 二、如何在生活中经历上帝的话语
title.en: II. How to encounter God’s word in daily life

blocks.zh: 那我们如何在现实生活中经历上帝的rhema呢？一、我们平时默想咀嚼神的话语，感受到当下神透过经文对我们的引导。二、我们在用心灵和诚实对上帝的敬拜中，感受到上帝对自己生命的说话。三、我们在主日听道或者特会中听到牧者的教导，感受到好像上帝在透过讲员对自己生命说话。四、其他，包含梦境或者超自然地听见上帝的说话和看见上帝给予的异象。
blocks.en: So how do we experience God’s rhema in real life? First, as we meditate and chew on God’s word, we sense God’s guidance through the Scripture in the present moment. Second, in worshipping God in spirit and in truth, we sense God speaking to our lives. Third, while listening to preaching on Sunday or at special meetings, we sense that God is speaking to us through the preacher. Fourth, other ways, including dreams or hearing God’s voice supernaturally and seeing visions God gives.

blocks.zh: 不管上帝使用哪一种方式对我们生命说话，都会建立我们的信心。但是话语也要查验，我们常常会在教会听到有人说，上帝和自己说了什么话语。需要查验之后才和弟兄姐妹或者牧者分享。例如，曾有弟兄对喜欢的姐妹说，“上帝说让你嫁给我。”
blocks.en: Whatever way God uses to speak to our lives, it builds our faith. But words must also be tested. In church we often hear people say that God told them something. They should test it before sharing it with brothers and sisters or with pastors. For example, a brother once told a sister he liked, "God said you are to marry me."

blocks.zh: 这叫人怎么回应是好呢？如果真的你听到某种类似的话语，你需要查验和等候，当上帝真的带领你们建立好关系并进入到婚姻当中的时候，你再分享出来比较好。而如果你到处大张嘴巴，不论是不是上帝对你说话，你都让自己和别人陷入到尴尬的光景当中了。
blocks.en: How should one respond to such a statement? If you really hear something like this, you need to test it and wait. When God truly leads you into a mature relationship and into marriage, then you can share it. But if you spread it everywhere, whether or not God actually spoke, you put yourself and others in an awkward position.

blocks.zh: 圣经中的马利亚总是把上帝的启示存在心里，当牧羊人找到马利亚和约瑟传递天使的言语说，大卫的城里为你们生了救主，就是主基督，你们要看见一个婴孩，包着布，卧在马槽里，这就是记号。很多人听见就很诧异，而马利亚就把这一切的事情存在心里。（路加福音二章）马利亚没有到处和别人讲，要求别人为自己的儿子做什么事情。
blocks.en: Mary in the Bible always treasured God’s revelations in her heart. When the shepherds found Mary and Joseph and passed on the angel’s words—that a Savior, Christ the Lord, had been born in the city of David, and the sign would be a baby wrapped in swaddling cloths lying in a manger—many who heard were amazed, but Mary treasured up all these things in her heart (Luke 2). Mary did not go around telling everyone and demanding things for her son.

blocks.zh: 用只有自己能听见的上帝说的话语要求别人做某事，真的会让人很反感！圣经的教导我们要顺服，在圣经以外，如果你真的听见什么话语，你要学会等候和查验，如果和别人有关，你也需要给别人查验你说的话语是与不是的机会。而如果是圣经中已经明确的教导，你不要说，让我祷告查验一下。
blocks.en: Using a word you alone claim to have heard from God to demand things from others truly repels people! The Bible teaches us to obey. Outside of Scripture, if you really hear something, learn to wait and test; if it involves others, you also need to give them the opportunity to test whether your word is from God. But if it is already a clear teaching of Scripture, do not say, "Let me pray and test it."

blocks.zh: 对于特殊的启示，你要给予自己和他人查验的机会；对于圣经的教导，你需要学习顺服和跟随，而不是用查验的借口来抵挡神的话语。
blocks.en: For special revelations, give yourself and others room to test; for the teachings of Scripture, learn to obey and follow, and do not use "testing" as an excuse to resist God’s word.

blocks.zh: 我们说上帝正在对我们说的话语叫做“rhema”，是带着能力的，是会建造我们信心的！在教会里你还会听到一个词语叫“logos”也是指上帝的话语。我们看一处经文。
blocks.en: We say the word God is speaking to us now is "rhema"—it carries power and builds our faith! In church you will also hear the word "logos," which also refers to God’s word. Let us look at a passage.

blocks.zh: 马太福音八章8节，这里的“一句话”原文发音就是“logos {log'-os}”。意思是说出来的话语或者承诺、宣告等。有人说，rhema是正在说的话语，是带着能力的，logos是已经说过的话语，没有rhema那么好！其实神的话语都有能力！
blocks.en: In Matthew 8:8, the Greek behind "the word" is "logos"—a spoken word, a promise, or a declaration. Some say rhema is the word being spoken now, carrying power, while logos is the word already spoken and not as good. In fact, all of God’s word carries power!

blocks.zh: rhema是当下领受到上帝的引导，logos是上帝说过的话语和原则。当下上帝正在说的时候叫rhema，当你回顾上帝的rhema的时候，这个话语已经是logos了。
blocks.en: rhema is the guidance you receive from God in the present; logos is the word and principles God has spoken. When God is speaking now, it is rhema; when you look back at God’s rhema, that word has already become logos.

blocks.zh: 希腊文的这些词语总是很绕人，容易让人迷糊。所以你会看见希腊有很多哲学大家。我们不要被词语绕住，上帝的rhema有能力，可以建造我们的信心，上帝的logos也能够叫百夫长的仆人立刻得到医治。关键的一点就是你要领受、接受、顺服，因为降服在上帝的话语之下，神的话语就会有能力来医治释放你！就会来建造你的生命、树立你的信心！
blocks.en: These Greek terms can be confusing. That is why Greece produced so many great philosophers. Do not get tangled up in words: God’s rhema has power to build our faith, and God’s logos could immediately heal the centurion’s servant. The key is to receive, accept, and obey—because when you submit to God’s word, it has power to heal and set you free, to build your life and establish your faith!

blocks.zh: rhema可以变成logos，logos也可以成为rhema。上帝对你说的话语，你不跟随也会成为过去的记忆而已；圣经中已经记载很多年的话语，你若是跟随也会成为对你生命吹气的rhema。
blocks.en: rhema can become logos, and logos can become rhema. A word God speaks to you, if you do not follow it, becomes a memory of the past; a word recorded in the Bible for many years, if you follow it, can become rhema breathing life into you.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 8:8
zh.text: 百夫长回答说：“主啊，你到我舍下，我不敢当；只要你说一句话，我的仆人就必好了。”

en.label: Scripture · Matthew 8:8
en.text: But the centurion replied, "Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, but only say the word, and my servant will be healed."

title.zh: 四、如何查验领受的话语
title.en: IV. How to test the word you receive

blocks.zh: 我们如何查验我们领受的是不是上帝对我们说的话语呢？在经文以外的，或者明显和神的话语相背离的确信，都不是圣经所说的信心，与圣经相背离的确信，可能是从人而来的美好的期待。
blocks.en: How do we test whether what we receive is really God’s word to us? Convictions outside of Scripture, or those that clearly contradict God’s word, are not the faith Scripture speaks of. A conviction that contradicts the Bible may be a good expectation that comes from man.

blocks.zh: 而你的期待虽然好，但你若不相信神的话语，就是期待经文中的应许发生在自己身上，如果你只是期待它发生、希望它发生，虽然你的希望是美好的，但希望和期待其实都不是信心。
blocks.en: Your expectation may be good, but if you do not believe God’s word—that is, if you merely expect the promises in Scripture to happen to you—if you only wish for them and hope for them, however beautiful your hope is, hope and expectation are not faith.

blocks.zh: 只有你全人、全心地相信，神的话语才会成为建造你信心的rhema；三心二意地对待神的话语是不会建立我们的信心的。
blocks.en: Only when you believe with your whole being and whole heart does God’s word become rhema that builds your faith. Treating God’s word half-heartedly will never build our faith.

title.zh: 五、什么是全人全心的相信？
title.en: V. What does whole-hearted believing mean?

blocks.zh: 信心其实不仅仅在我们思想中与我们互动！信心在我们思想中，但不只是在思想中。你不能只是希望美好的事发生在你生命中！而是你要对神的话语，用理性确认是真实的！用情感盼望神的话语，一定会成就在自己生命中！用意志去降服神的话语、跟随神的话语。
blocks.en: Faith does not merely interact with us in our thoughts. Faith lives in our minds, but not only in our minds. You cannot merely wish for good things to happen in your life! Rather, toward God’s word you must confirm with your reason that it is true, hope with your emotions that it will surely be fulfilled in your life, and submit with your will and follow it.

blocks.zh: 理性、情感、意志对神话语的顺服，这三点都是不可少的。
blocks.en: Reason, emotion, and will all submitting to God’s word—these three are all indispensable.

blocks.zh: 你不能只是在情感中期待事情按照神的话语发生！如果没有理性的认知和意志的顺服，你情感上的期待只是希望。就好像生病的时候说，“我真的希望我得医治就好了！”这样不能说是信心！
blocks.en: You cannot merely hope with your emotions that things will happen according to God’s word. Without rational understanding and willing obedience, your emotional hope is only wishing. Like a sick person saying, "I really hope I get healed!"—that cannot be called faith.

blocks.zh: 你也不能只是理性上知道上帝是医治我们的神！情感上却一点也不期待，沮丧得好像你马上就死了，你能够说这是有信心的吗？
blocks.en: Nor can you only know in your mind that God is our healer, yet feel no hope in your heart, depressed as if you were about to die. Can you call that faith?

blocks.zh: 你也不能只是说，“顺服就蒙福。”“我要跟随神！”“我要守主日！”“我要奉献！”如果你没有对上帝理性的认知与情感上的盼望，你顺服上帝的话语会很干枯！你好像感觉自己的灵性快要死了！对上帝的事情好像缺少兴趣。
blocks.en: Nor can you only say, "Obedience brings blessing. I will follow God! I will keep the Lord’s Day! I will give!" Without rational knowledge of God and emotional hope, your obedience to God’s word becomes dry. It feels like your spiritual life is dying, and you seem to lose interest in the things of God.

blocks.zh: 但如果你有意志上对上帝的顺服，加上理性上对上帝的认识，再加上经历上帝的真实！你就会生发出情感上的盼望，好像不论现在你经历怎样的环境，你都相信上帝在掌权，最终一定会有不一样的结局，你才能去爱上帝，才能在意志上更多地顺服上帝、爱上帝。阿们！
blocks.en: But if you have obedience of the will toward God, added to rational knowledge of God, plus experiencing God’s reality, then emotional hope is kindled. Whatever circumstances you face, you believe God is in control, and the end will surely be different. Then you can love God and submit to Him and love Him all the more. Amen!

blocks.zh: 我们最后读两节经文。信就是所望之事的实底，是未见之事的确据；凡你们祷告祈求的，无论是什么，只要信是得着的，就必得着。愿上帝的话语建造我们的信心！
blocks.en: Let us read two more verses. Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen; and whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours. May God’s word build our faith!

zh.label: 圣经 · 希伯来书 11:1
zh.text: 信就是所望之事的实底，是未见之事的确据。

en.label: Scripture · Hebrews 11:1
en.text: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 11:24
zh.text: 所以我告诉你们：凡你们祷告祈求的，无论是什么，只要信是得着的，就必得着。

en.label: Scripture · Mark 11:24
en.text: Therefore I tell you, whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.

verse.en: You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and the fourth generation.<small>Deuteronomy 5:9</small>

verseText.zh: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可侍奉它们，因为我耶和华你的神是忌邪的神。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三四代
verseText.en: You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and the fourth generation.

summary.zh: 从使徒行传对外邦信徒的禁戒（禁戒偶像的污秽和奸淫，并勒死的牲畜和血）讲起：申命记中制造偶像、跪拜偶像、带偶像之物进家、行邪术占卜所带下的咒诅；说明拜偶像如何给邪灵留下破口、成为累代咒诅与家族性邪灵的转移；剖析拜祖先牌位、算命、被献作假神义子等破口；最后给出砍断家族咒诅的六个阶段——清理当灭之物、站在破口为祖先认罪、彻底饶恕、废除与邪灵的约定、捆绑壮士斥责邪灵、持守自由的属灵守望操练。附 4 个思考问题。
summary.en: Beginning with the apostles’ instruction to Gentile believers (to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, and from what has been strangled and from blood), this sermon explains the curses brought by making idols, bowing down to them, bringing idol-related objects into the home, and practicing sorcery and divination. It shows how idolatry opens a breach for evil spirits, becoming a generational curse and the transfer of family spirits. It examines breaches such as worshipping ancestral tablets, fortune-telling, and being dedicated as adopted children to false gods. Finally, it gives six stages for breaking family curses—removing devoted things, standing in the breach to confess the sins of ancestors, thoroughly forgiving, revoking agreements made with evil spirits, binding the strong man and commanding spirits to leave, and persevering in spiritual watchfulness in freedom. With 4 reflection questions.

blocks.zh: 最近在回顾我们教会的讲道内容，我发现关于“偶像和咒诅”方面的内容几乎没有，而这个方面的教导又是比较重要的；在使徒行传中说到，对于信主的外邦人来说，“拜偶像”是其中一个禁忌。所以，对于我们外邦教会来说，这方面的教导就显得尤为重要了。
blocks.en: Recently, while reviewing the sermons of our church, I noticed there is almost nothing on "idols and curses," yet this area of teaching is quite important. In Acts, the apostles said that for believing Gentiles, "idolatry" was one of the forbidden things. For a Gentile church like ours, this teaching is therefore especially important.

blocks.zh: 使徒行传十五章说到的是：“禁戒偶像的污秽和奸淫，并勒死的牲畜和血”；使徒行传二十一章说到的是：“祭偶像之物和血，并勒死的牲畜与奸淫。”综合来看，和偶像有关的禁戒占了四分之一。禁戒偶像的污秽，说的是禁止基督徒食用祭偶像的物品，也禁止基督徒祭拜偶像。
blocks.en: Acts 15 says: "abstain from the things polluted by idols, and from sexual immorality, and from what has been strangled, and from blood." Acts 21 says: "what has been sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality." Taken together, prohibitions related to idols make up a quarter of the list. Abstaining from things polluted by idols means Christians must not eat food offered to idols, and must not worship idols either.

zh.label: 圣经 · 使徒行传 15:20
zh.text: 只要写信吩咐他们禁戒偶像的污秽和奸淫，并勒死的牲畜和血。

en.label: Scripture · Acts 15:20
en.text: But should write to them to abstain from the things polluted by idols, and from sexual immorality, and from what has been strangled, and from blood.

zh.label: 圣经 · 使徒行传 21:25
zh.text: 至于信主的外邦人，我们已经写信拟定，叫他们谨忌那祭偶像之物和血，并勒死的牲畜与奸淫。

en.label: Scripture · Acts 21:25
en.text: But as for the Gentiles who have believed, we have sent a letter with our judgment that they should abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what has been strangled, and from sexual immorality.

blocks.zh: 从申命记的几处经文可以看到，制造偶像的人必定承受咒诅；跪拜偶像，上帝要追讨他的罪，从父亲到儿子，直到三四代；把和偶像有关联的物品带到家中也不可以，会与物品一样成为当灭之物；而算命、占卜、邪术、巫术、交鬼、通灵等，都是上帝所憎恶的。
blocks.en: From these passages in Deuteronomy we see that whoever makes idols certainly bears a curse; whoever bows down to idols—God visits his iniquity on him from father to son to the third and fourth generation; bringing idol-related objects into the home is also forbidden, making one devoted to destruction like the object itself; and fortune-telling, divination, sorcery, witchcraft, mediums, and spiritism are all an abomination to God.

blocks.zh: 从这里可以整理出四个类别：制造偶像、跪拜偶像、拥有和偶像有关的物品，以及其他和偶像背后邪灵有关的行为——都可以归到“拜偶像”这个类别中来。上帝厌恶这样的行为，并且这些行为会带下咒诅。
blocks.en: From this we can sort out four categories: making idols, bowing down to idols, possessing objects connected with idols, and other practices connected with the spirits behind idols—all fall under "idolatry." God detests these practices, and they bring down a curse.

blocks.zh: 不是上帝故意要咒诅人，而是这些行为给了背后的邪灵破口，来辖制陷在其中的人。
blocks.en: It is not that God deliberately curses people, but that these practices give the spirits behind them a breach to control those caught in them.

blocks.zh: 人不能既敬拜神又敬拜偶像，因为神是忌邪的神。拜偶像带来世代追讨的咒诅：不可雕刻并跪拜偶像，因为神必追讨拜偶像（恨神）之人的罪，“自父及子，直到三四代”。这种由于祖先犯罪而代代传递下来的咒诅，会带下鬼魔的辖制与悲剧，我们称之为“累代的咒诅”。
blocks.en: A person cannot both worship God and worship idols, for God is a jealous God. Idolatry brings a curse pursued across generations: you must not carve or bow down to idols, for God will visit the iniquity of those who worship idols (who hate God) "to the third and the fourth generation." This curse, passed from generation to generation because of ancestors’ sin, brings demonic bondage and tragedy. We call it a "generational curse."

blocks.zh: 拜偶像或者违背上帝的话语，会主动为仇敌敞开大门（留地步）：魔鬼或者邪灵、污鬼无法强迫人，除非人主动给它机会。当人参与偶像崇拜、行邪术、算命或与假神立约时，实际上是在灵界与黑暗权势合作，在生命中开了破口（留了地步），给邪灵提供了合法在家族中盘踞、生根的契约与权利。
blocks.en: Idolatry or disobedience to God’s word actively opens a door (gives ground) to the enemy: the devil, evil spirits, or unclean spirits cannot force anyone unless the person actively gives them an opportunity. When a person participates in idol worship, sorcery, fortune-telling, or makes covenants with false gods, he is in reality cooperating with dark powers in the spiritual realm, opening a breach (giving ground) in his life, and providing evil spirits with a lawful contract and right to dwell and take root in the family.

zh.label: 圣经 · 申命记 27:15
zh.text: “有人制造耶和华所憎恶的偶像，或雕刻，或铸造，就是工匠手所作的，在暗中设立，那人必受咒诅！”百姓都要答应说：“阿们！”

en.label: Scripture · Deuteronomy 27:15
en.text: Cursed be the man who makes a carved or cast metal image, an abomination to the LORD, a thing made by the hands of a craftsman, and sets it up in secret. And all the people shall answer and say, "Amen."

zh.label: 圣经 · 申命记 5:9
zh.text: 不可跪拜那些像，也不可侍奉它们，因为我耶和华你的神是忌邪的神。恨我的，我必追讨他的罪，自父及子，直到三四代。

en.label: Scripture · Deuteronomy 5:9
en.text: You shall not bow down to them or serve them, for I the LORD your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children to the third and the fourth generation.

zh.label: 圣经 · 申命记 7:26
zh.text: 可憎的物，你不可带进家去，不然，你就成了当毁灭的，与那物一样。你要十分厌恶、十分憎嫌，因为这是当毁灭的物。

en.label: Scripture · Deuteronomy 7:26
en.text: And you shall not bring an abominable thing into your house, lest you become devoted to destruction like it. You shall utterly detest and abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.

zh.label: 圣经 · 申命记 18:10–12
zh.text: 你们中间不可有人使儿女经火，也不可有占卜的、观兆的、用法术的、行邪术的、用迷术的、交鬼的、行巫术的、过阴的。凡行这些事的，都为耶和华所憎恶，因那些国民行这可憎恶的事，所以耶和华你的神将他们从你面前赶出。

en.label: Scripture · Deuteronomy 18:10–12
en.text: There shall not be found among you anyone who burns his son or his daughter as an offering, anyone who practices divination or tells fortunes or interprets omens, or a sorcerer, or a charmer, or a medium, or a necromancer, or one who inquires of the dead. For whoever does these things is an abomination to the LORD. And because of these abominations the LORD your God is driving them out before you.

title.zh: 二、拜偶像会成为家族的咒诅
title.en: II. Idolatry becomes a familial curse

blocks.zh: 一旦祖先通过拜偶像给仇敌留了合法的破口，邪灵便会顺理成章地进入并长期滞留于该家族中。圣经说，自父及子直到三四代。
blocks.en: Once an ancestor leaves a lawful breach to the enemy through idolatry, evil spirits enter and remain in that family for a long time as a matter of course. The Bible says: from father to son, to the third and fourth generation.

blocks.zh: 邪灵的“搬家”与转移：这些在祖先拜偶像时被迎进来的邪灵，被称为家族性邪灵。现在的动漫影视作品会美化这种鬼魔附身，通常宿主会得到附身灵的能力，然后在影视剧中开始“开挂人生”。
blocks.en: The "moving house" and transfer of evil spirits: these spirits welcomed in when ancestors worshipped idols are called familial spirits. Modern anime and films romanticize demon possession—usually the host gains the power of the indwelling spirit and then begins a "cheat-code life" in the story.

blocks.zh: 因为邪灵是灵体，在物质世界中极度渴望寻找人体居住。当拜偶像的祖先去世时，这些邪灵不会消失，而是会寻找血亲作为新的居所，通过母亲怀孕、生产或亲人死亡等时机，转移到子孙后代身上。
blocks.en: Because evil spirits are spiritual beings, they desperately seek human bodies to inhabit in the material world. When an ancestor who worshipped idols dies, these spirits do not disappear; they seek blood relatives as new dwellings, transferring to descendants through opportunities such as a mother’s pregnancy, childbirth, or the death of a loved one.

blocks.zh: 圣经说，污鬼就是邪灵，只有在人的身上才能得到安歇，而离开人他们得不到安歇。所以，如果有机会它不会愿意离开人。
blocks.en: The Bible says an unclean spirit is an evil spirit; it finds rest only in a human being, and away from people it finds no rest. So if it has the chance, it will not leave a person.

blocks.zh: 污鬼不会愿意离开被附身的宿主，因为它把宿主的身体当成自己的房屋、自己的家。污鬼和邪灵是附身在人体邪恶力量的两种不同描述的名称。
blocks.en: An unclean spirit will not willingly leave the host it possesses, because it treats the host’s body as its house, its home. "Unclean spirit" and "evil spirit" are two names describing evil forces that attach themselves to human bodies.

blocks.zh: 而魔鬼或者撒旦是堕落的天使。从圣经文本的角度来看，污鬼和邪灵的来源圣经没有明确的指出来，但污鬼和邪灵渴望附身在人的身上，而身为堕落天使的魔鬼却没有这个需要。
blocks.en: The devil, or Satan, is a fallen angel. From the biblical text, the origin of unclean and evil spirits is not clearly stated; but unclean and evil spirits long to attach themselves to people, while the devil, as a fallen angel, has no such need.

blocks.zh: 偶像崇拜带下的咒诅就和邪灵或者污鬼有关，而这些邪灵会了解这个家族的人性弱点，在弱点上加以蛊惑，让这个被蛊惑的成员沉溺在这些人性的弱点中，被邪恶力量辖制、捆绑。
blocks.en: The curse brought by idol worship is connected with evil spirits or unclean spirits. These spirits learn the human weaknesses of a family and seduce through those weaknesses, causing the ensnared member to sink into them, bound and controlled by evil forces.

blocks.zh: 邪灵会在后代处于软弱（如焦虑、沮丧、害怕）时进行引诱与攻击，导致特定的犯罪模式（如酗酒、暴力、淫乱、赌博）或特定疾病在家族中代代相传、甚至隔代遗传。
blocks.en: Evil spirits tempt and attack descendants in their weakness (such as anxiety, depression, or fear), causing particular patterns of sin (such as alcoholism, violence, sexual immorality, or gambling) or particular diseases to be passed down through generations, sometimes skipping one.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 12:43
zh.text: 污鬼离了人身，就在无水之地过来过去，寻求安歇之处，却寻不着。

en.label: Scripture · Matthew 12:43
en.text: When the unclean spirit has gone out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, but finds none.

title.zh: 三、拜偶像的破口和辖制
title.en: III. The breaches and bondage of idolatry

blocks.zh: 将祖先当假神膜拜的破口：我们传统风俗会去膜拜去世的祖先牌位。拜偶像和拜祖先，是我们祖先传承下来最大的两个辖制和破口，这也导致后代极易受到累代咒诅的捆绑，这也是以弗所书所说的“风俗背后的邪灵对人的辖制”。
blocks.en: The breach of worshipping ancestors as false gods: our traditional customs lead us to worship the memorial tablets of the dead. Idolatry and ancestor worship are the two greatest bondages and breaches handed down by our ancestors, making descendants extremely vulnerable to the grip of generational curses. This is what Ephesians calls "the spirit that is now at work in the sons of disobedience" behind worldly customs.

blocks.zh: 无知沾染带来的辖制：许多人因为无知，在成长过程中随从民俗参与算命、占卜、玩碟仙，甚至在幼年时被父母献给妈祖或观音当义子、义女。
blocks.en: Bondage from ignorant involvement: many people, out of ignorance, followed folk customs while growing up—fortune-telling, divination, playing with spirit-writing (ouija), even being dedicated by their parents in childhood as adopted sons or daughters of Matsu or Guanyin.

blocks.zh: 这些与偶像立约的行为，都为黑暗权势提供了合法的管道来操纵和破坏人的生活。
blocks.en: These covenant-making practices with idols provide the powers of darkness with a lawful channel to manipulate and destroy people’s lives.

zh.label: 圣经 · 以弗所书 2:2
zh.text: 那时，你们在其中行事为人，随从今世的风俗，顺服空中掌权者的首领，就是现今在悖逆之子心中运行的邪灵。

en.label: Scripture · Ephesians 2:2
en.text: In which you once walked, following the course of this world, following the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that is now at work in the sons of disobedience.

title.zh: 四、如何砍断拜偶像带来的家族咒诅？
title.en: IV. How do we break the familial curses of idolatry?

blocks.zh: 虽然耶稣基督在十字架上已经承担了律法的咒诅，赎出了我们，但要使这救赎在个人生命中实际产生免除咒诅的效力，必须主动配合进行属灵的清理：
blocks.en: Although Jesus Christ already bore the curse of the law on the cross and redeemed us, for this redemption to actually take effect in a personal life by removing the curse, one must actively cooperate in spiritual cleansing:

blocks.zh: 属灵原理：邪灵是没有形体的灵，它们极其喜欢和它们有连接的物件来依附。在家中保留算命书、佛珠、护身符、招财猫、易经八卦资料，甚至色情和暴力的物品，都会让邪灵有合法的地位与权利来盘踞。
blocks.en: Spiritual principle: evil spirits are bodiless spirits; they love to cling to objects connected with them. Keeping fortune-telling books, prayer beads, amulets, lucky cats, I-Ching and Bagua materials, or even pornographic and violent objects in the home gives evil spirits a lawful standing and right to dwell.

blocks.zh: 实操祷告与行动：在清理前，请求耶稣宝血遮盖与保护；动手搜寻并彻底丢弃、烧毁或打碎家中所有与偶像、算命占卜、气功异端有关的实体物品。
blocks.en: Practical prayer and action: before cleaning, ask for the covering and protection of the blood of Jesus; search and thoroughly discard, burn, or smash all physical objects in the home connected with idols, fortune-telling, divination, or cultic qigong.

blocks.zh: 属灵原理：我们可以根据圣经经文站在破口上代替我们的血亲祖先向神认罪悔改，求主耶稣的宝血堵住因祖先犯罪（如拜偶像、拜祖先牌位、流无辜人血、情欲、淫乱暴力等）而给魔鬼留下的世代合法破口。
blocks.en: Spiritual principle: based on Scripture we may stand in the breach on behalf of our blood relatives and ancestors, confessing and repenting before God, asking that the blood of Jesus would seal the lawful breach left to the devil by the sins of ancestors (such as idolatry, worship of ancestral tablets, shedding innocent blood, lust, sexual immorality, and violence).

blocks.zh: 根据民风、民俗（拜观音、妈祖、关公、土地公、祭拜祖先牌位、算命、过火等）进行具体的认罪祷告。
blocks.en: Offer specific prayers of confession according to the folk customs of the region (worshipping Guanyin, Matsu, Guan Gong, the Earth God, ancestral tablets, fortune-telling, fire-walking, and so on).

blocks.zh: 属灵原理：不饶恕、仇恨与苦毒是撒但在人们生命中得以立足、魔鬼盘踞的最主要“合法破口”之一。如果不从心里饶恕伤害过我们的父母、长辈或他人，仇敌在灵界就有话可说，使释放工作陷入僵局。
blocks.en: Spiritual principle: unforgiveness, hatred, and bitterness are among the chief "lawful breaches" by which Satan gains a foothold and demons dwell in people’s lives. If we do not forgive from the heart those parents, elders, or others who have hurt us, the enemy has something to say in the spiritual realm, and the work of deliverance reaches a standstill.

blocks.zh: 饶恕与释放祷告：大声在神面前以意志力决定饶恕曾经深深伤害、虐待过自己的长辈、父母或其他人，弃绝对其进行报复或咒诅的念头，转而以祝福取代。
blocks.en: Prayer of forgiveness and release: before God, loudly decide with your will to forgive the elders, parents, or others who have deeply hurt or abused you; renounce every thought of revenge or cursing them, and instead replace it with blessing.

blocks.zh: 属灵原理：在成长过程中，可能因父母的无知而被献给妈祖或观世音等假神当“义子义女”（契孙），或自己曾对某些偶像、玩偶、虚拟朋友许过愿或立过誓。这些立约给邪灵提供了合法操纵人的契约。
blocks.en: Spiritual principle: while growing up, because of parents’ ignorance you may have been dedicated to false gods such as Matsu or Guanyin as an "adopted son or daughter," or you yourself may have made vows or sworn oaths to certain idols, dolls, or imaginary friends. These covenants provide evil spirits with a contract to lawfully manipulate you.

blocks.zh: 破除和仇敌立约的祷告：奉耶稣的名宣告这些曾被私下或公开立下的约定，已被主耶稣在十字架上的宝血完全废止、涂抹并断开，宣告自己的身体不属于观世音或任何偶像，乃是属于圣灵的殿。
blocks.en: Prayer breaking covenants with the enemy: declare in the name of Jesus that these covenants made privately or publicly have been fully annulled, blotted out, and broken by the blood of Jesus on the cross; declare that your body does not belong to Guanyin or any idol, but is the temple of the Holy Spirit.

blocks.zh: 捆绑壮士与赶鬼祷告：依照马太福音十二章29节“先捆绑壮士”，奉耶稣基督的名宣告在十字架上的得胜，命令特定的家族性邪灵（如酒精邪灵、贫穷灵、凶恶灵、情欲蛇灵、死亡灵）立刻离开自己，并且宣告不准它们碰下一代子孙。
blocks.en: Prayer binding the strong man and casting out demons: according to Matthew 12:29, "first bind the strong man"; declare in the name of Jesus Christ the victory of the cross, and command specific familial spirits (such as the spirit of alcohol, the spirit of poverty, the spirit of violence, the snake spirit of lust, the spirit of death) to leave you immediately, and declare that they may not touch the next generation of descendants.

blocks.zh: 持守秘诀：释放祷告完毕后，请求耶稣和神的爱，充满原先被恶者盘踞的心中和身体空处，永不离开。
blocks.en: The secret of holding fast: after the prayer of release is finished, ask Jesus and the love of God to fill the empty places in your heart and body that were previously occupied by the evil one, and never to leave.

blocks.zh: 意志力的操练：随时操练自我意志，一有引诱立刻在心思意念中奉主名大声抵挡。
blocks.en: Training the will: practice self-control at all times; at the first sign of temptation, resist loudly in your thoughts and intentions in the name of the Lord.

blocks.zh: 三股合成的绳子：每天坚持稳定且大量的读经、强有力的祷告，在房里播放并同唱十字架与赞美诗歌，同时积极参与小组和肢体教会生活，防备仇敌借由“疑惑、害怕、不饶恕”等手段进行反扑。
blocks.en: A threefold cord: daily persist in steady and abundant reading of Scripture, powerful prayer, playing and singing along with hymns of the cross and praise in your home, while actively participating in small groups and the life of the local church—guarding against the enemy’s counterattack through means such as "doubt, fear, and unforgiveness."

zh.label: 圣经 · 利未记 26:40
zh.text: 他们要承认自己的罪和他们祖宗的罪，就是干犯我的那罪；并且承认自己行事与我反对。

en.label: Scripture · Leviticus 26:40
en.text: But if they confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers in their treachery that they committed against me, and also in walking contrary to me.

zh.label: 圣经 · 尼希米记 1:6
zh.text: 愿你睁眼看，侧耳听你仆人昼夜在你面前为你众仆人以色列民的祈祷，承认我们以色列人向你所犯的罪。我与我父家都有罪了。

en.label: Scripture · Nehemiah 1:6
en.text: Let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant that I now pray before you day and night for the people of Israel your servants, confessing the sins of the people of Israel, which we have sinned against you. Even I and my father’s house have sinned.

zh.label: 圣经 · 尼希米记 9:2
zh.text: 以色列人就与一切外邦人离绝，站着承认自己的罪恶和列祖的罪孽。

en.label: Scripture · Nehemiah 9:2
en.text: And the Israelites separated themselves from all foreigners and stood and confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 12:29
zh.text: 人怎能进壮士家里，抢夺他的家具呢？除非先捆住那壮士，才可以抢夺他的家财。

en.label: Scripture · Matthew 12:29
en.text: Or how can someone enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? Then indeed he may plunder his house.

blocks.zh: 拜偶像和犯罪会带下仇敌的咒诅，但是耶稣基督担当了我们的咒诅。我们只要接受耶稣成为我们生命的救主，离弃偶像、丢弃偶像的物品，奉主耶稣的名捆绑邪灵，命令它们离开自己和自己的家庭，宣告自己是属于耶稣基督！并且从此开始跟随耶稣基督，仇敌就无法辖制自己。
blocks.en: Idolatry and sin bring down the enemy’s curse, but Jesus Christ has borne our curse. If we only accept Jesus as the Savior of our lives, turn away from idols, discard idolatrous objects, bind evil spirits in the name of the Lord Jesus, command them to leave us and our families, and declare that we belong to Jesus Christ—and from then on follow Jesus Christ—the enemy can no longer control us.

生活中有哪些容易被忽略的“隐形偶像”或民俗物品（如算命书、招财猫）？我们该如何彻底清理它们？
你观察到自己或身边家族有哪些代代相传的“弱点”（如焦虑、特定疾病、酗酒等）？我们可以如何靠主打破它？
面对非信徒家人的传统民俗要求（如拜祖先、幼年时作假神义子），我们该如何既坚持信仰原则又尽到孝道？
为什么在断开家族咒诅时，“饶恕长辈”和“代祖先认罪”如此重要？这对你最大的挑战是什么？
blocks.en:
What "hidden idols" or folk objects in daily life are easily overlooked (such as fortune-telling books or lucky cats)? How should we thoroughly remove them?
What weaknesses passed down through generations have you observed in yourself or in family lines (such as anxiety, particular diseases, alcoholism)? How can we break them by the Lord?

title.zh: 天堂和地狱和“我”有什么关系吗？
title.en: What Does Heaven and Hell Have to Do with Me?

verse.zh: 神就是爱，住在爱里面的，就是住在神里面，神也住在他里面<small>约翰一书 4:16</small>
verse.en: God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them<small>1 John 4:16</small>

verseText.zh: 神就是爱，住在爱里面的，就是住在神里面，神也住在他里面
verseText.en: God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them

summary.zh: 从“上帝是慈爱的，为什么不信祂的人要下地狱受苦”的疑问说起：梳理圣经中关于地狱和阴间的词语——欣嫩子谷（新约“地狱”的来源）、塔塔鲁斯（天使被囚之地）、阴间/哈迪斯（不信者死后暂时受苦之处）、乐园（得救者的去处）与火湖（第二次的死）；再讲天堂与神的国——神的国就在你们心里，现在就要活在天堂里，活在神的爱中；最后用叛逆孩子拒绝父母之爱的比喻，说明不是上帝要人受苦，而是拒绝上帝的爱使人痛苦，活在仇恨苦毒中就像浅尝地狱的滋味。附 4 个思考问题。
summary.en: Starting from the question "God is loving, so why do those who do not believe in Him suffer in hell?": sorting out the Bible's words about hell and Hades — the Valley of Hinnom (the origin of "hell" in the New Testament), Tartarus (where fallen angels are held), Hades (where the unbelieving suffer temporarily after death), Paradise (the dwelling of the saved) and the Lake of Fire (the second death); then about heaven and the kingdom of God — the kingdom of God is within you, you must live in heaven now, living in God's love; finally, using the parable of the rebellious child who rejects his parents' love, showing that it is not God who makes people suffer, but rejecting God's love brings pain — living in hatred and bitterness is like a foretaste of hell. With 4 questions for reflection.

blocks.zh: 有时候，我会听到有人说，“基督徒说，上帝是有慈爱的上帝，为什么不信祂的人就要下地狱受苦？”并且越讲越对基督教信仰产生不满，也越发不肯接受基督的信仰。
blocks.en: Sometimes I hear people say, "Christians say God is a God of love, so why do those who do not believe in Him have to suffer in hell?" And the more they talk about it, the more dissatisfied they become with the Christian faith, and the more unwilling they are to accept the faith of Christ.

title.en: Valley of Hinnom — Where "Hell" Comes From

blocks.zh: “地狱”这个词语从旧约圣经的一个地名“欣嫩子谷”演化而来。在旧约圣经中记载以色列在这个地方效法迦南人的习俗，在这个地方给外邦的鬼神烧香，并把自己的婴孩作为祭品焚烧给邪神。
blocks.en: The word "hell" comes from a place name in the Old Testament, the "Valley of Hinnom." The Old Testament records that Israel imitated the customs of the Canaanites in this place, burning incense to foreign gods and even sacrificing their own children as burnt offerings to false gods.

blocks.zh: 这里的“地狱”，原文说的就是“欣嫩子谷”。新约圣经说的地狱，大部分用的词语是这个“欣嫩子谷”。
blocks.en: The "hell" mentioned here is, in the original language, the "Valley of Hinnom." Most of the time when the New Testament speaks of hell, it uses this word, "Valley of Hinnom."

zh.label: 圣经 · 历代志下 28:3
zh.text: 并且在欣嫩子谷烧香，用火焚烧他的儿女，行耶和华在以色列人面前所驱逐的外邦人那可憎的事。

en.label: Scripture · 2 Chronicles 28:3
en.text: He burned incense in the Valley of Hinnom and sacrificed his children in the fire, engaging in the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

zh.label: 圣经 · 耶利米书 32:35
zh.text: 他们在欣嫩子谷建筑巴力的邱坛，好使自己的儿女经火归摩洛，他们行这可憎的事，使犹大陷在罪里。这并不是我所吩咐的，也不是我心所起的意。

en.label: Scripture · Jeremiah 32:35
en.text: They built high places for Baal in the Valley of Hinnom to sacrifice their sons and daughters to Molek, though I never commanded—nor did it enter my mind—that they should do such a detestable thing and so make Judah sin.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 5:22
zh.text: 只是我告诉你们：凡向弟兄动怒的，难免受审判（有古卷在“凡”字下添“无缘无故地”五字）。凡骂弟兄是拉加的，难免公会的审断；凡骂弟兄是魔利的，难免地狱的火。

en.label: Scripture · Matthew 5:22
en.text: But I tell you that anyone who is angry with a brother or sister will be subject to judgment. Again, anyone who says to a brother or sister, "Raca," is answerable to the court. And anyone who says, "You fool!" will be in danger of the fire of hell.

title.zh: 塔塔鲁斯——天使被囚之地
title.en: Tartarus — Where Fallen Angels Are Held

blocks.zh: 这里的彼得说的地狱，源自“Tartaros”（音塔塔鲁斯）。希腊人认为比阴间还要低深的一处地方。彼得说，天使犯罪之后，就曾经被丢在这个地方。阴间是什么地方呢？
blocks.en: The hell Peter speaks of here comes from "Tartaros." The Greeks considered it a place deeper and lower than Hades. Peter says that after the angels sinned, they were cast into this place. So what is Hades?

zh.label: 圣经 · 彼得后书 2:4
zh.text: 就是天使犯了罪，神也没有宽容，曾把他们丢在地狱，交在黑暗坑中，等候审判。

en.label: Scripture · 2 Peter 2:4
en.text: For if God did not spare angels when they sinned, but sent them to hell, putting them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment...

title.en: Hades — A Place of Temporary Suffering

blocks.zh: 这里说的财主和乞丐拉撒路的例子，意思是不跟随神的财主，死后暂时受苦的地方叫“阴间”（音哈迪斯）。而拉撒路所在的地方是乐园，也是所有得救的人死后所在的地方。
blocks.en: In the account of the rich man and the beggar Lazarus, the place where the rich man who did not follow God suffers temporarily after death is called "Hades." The place where Lazarus was is Paradise, the place where all who are saved go after death.

blocks.zh: 我们整理一下刚刚所说的关于地狱和阴间的词语。其中一个是我们刚刚说的，叫“阴间 - 哈迪斯”。另外一个是“地狱 - 塔塔鲁斯”天使犯罪被关押的地方。最后一个是“地狱 - 欣嫩子谷”。
blocks.en: Let us sort out the words about hell and Hades we have just mentioned. One is what we just spoke of, "Hades." Another is "Hell — Tartarus," the place where angels who sinned are imprisoned. The last is "Hell — Valley of Hinnom."

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 16:23
zh.text: 他在阴间受痛苦，举目远远地望见亚伯拉罕，又望见拉撒路在他怀里。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 16:23
en.text: In Hades, where he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus by his side.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 23:43
zh.text: 耶稣对他说：“我实在告诉你：今日你要同我在乐园里了。”

en.label: Scripture · Luke 23:43
en.text: Jesus answered him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."

title.en: Lake of Fire — The Second Death

blocks.zh: 阴间和死亡会被丢在火湖里面焚烧，魔鬼、兽、假先知、名字没有被记录在生命册上的人，都会被丢在火湖里面，圣经说，这是第二次的死。
blocks.en: Hades and death will be cast into the lake of fire and burned. The devil, the beast, the false prophet, and everyone whose name is not written in the book of life will be cast into the lake of fire. The Bible calls this the second death.

zh.label: 圣经 · 启示录 20:10
zh.text: 那迷惑他们的魔鬼被扔在硫磺的火湖里，就是兽和假先知所在的地方。他们必昼夜受痛苦，直到永永远远。

en.label: Scripture · Revelation 20:10
en.text: And the devil, who deceived them, was thrown into the lake of burning sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet had been thrown. They will be tormented day and night for ever and ever.

zh.label: 圣经 · 启示录 20:13
zh.text: 于是海交出其中的死人，死亡和阴间也交出其中的死人。他们都照各人所行的受审判。

en.label: Scripture · Revelation 20:13
en.text: The sea gave up the dead that were in it, and death and Hades gave up the dead that were in them, and each person was judged according to what they had done.

zh.label: 圣经 · 启示录 20:14
zh.text: 死亡和阴间也被扔在火湖里，这火湖就是第二次的死。

en.label: Scripture · Revelation 20:14
en.text: Then death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. The lake of fire is the second death.

zh.label: 圣经 · 启示录 20:15
zh.text: 若有人名字没记在生命册上，他就被扔在火湖里。

en.label: Scripture · Revelation 20:15
en.text: Anyone whose name was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.

title.en: Paradise — The Dwelling of the Righteous

blocks.zh: 我们再说说，名字被记录在生命册子上的人，根据圣经记载，他们离开世界后，会先去到乐园里面。
blocks.en: Now let us talk about those whose names are written in the book of life. According to the Bible, after they leave this world, they first go to Paradise.

blocks.zh: “乐园”（Paradise）来源于古波斯语，意思是“有围墙的皇家园林。”
blocks.en: "Paradise" comes from ancient Persian, meaning "a walled royal garden."

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 23:43
zh.text: 耶稣对他说：“我实在告诉你：今日你要同我在乐园里了。”

en.label: Scripture · Luke 23:43
en.text: Jesus answered him, "Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise."

zh.label: 圣经 · 哥林多后书 12:4
zh.text: 他被提到乐园里，听见隐秘的言语，是人不可说的。

en.label: Scripture · 2 Corinthians 12:4
en.text: was caught up to paradise and heard inexpressible things, things that no one is permitted to tell.

zh.label: 圣经 · 启示录 2:7
zh.text: 圣灵向众教会所说的话，凡有耳的，就应当听。得胜的，我必将神乐园中生命树的果子赐给他吃。

en.label: Scripture · Revelation 2:7
en.text: Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who is victorious, I will give the right to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.

title.zh: 神的国——现在就能经历的天堂
title.en: Kingdom of God — Heaven You Can Experience Now

blocks.zh: 和“被神称为义的人”有关的另外一个词语是天堂，圣经中的天堂是“天上”，另外有两个词语是“天国”和“神的国”。
blocks.en: Another word related to "those justified by God" is heaven. In the Bible, heaven is "the heavens"; there are also two other words, "the kingdom of heaven" and "the kingdom of God."

blocks.zh: 我们来看基督徒现在就能经历到的天堂和将来要来到的天堂。
blocks.en: Let us look at the heaven that Christians can experience now, and the heaven that is yet to come.

blocks.zh: 神的国，这里的“国”和“天国”“神的国”的“国”是同一个词语，天国和神的国，强调的是“神掌权的国度”和“天上的国度”。当你进入天堂的时候，说的是进入神掌权的、天上的国度。
blocks.en: The "kingdom" here in "the kingdom of God" is the same word as in "the kingdom of heaven." "Kingdom of heaven" and "kingdom of God" emphasize "the realm where God reigns" and "the heavenly realm." When you enter heaven, it means entering the heavenly realm where God reigns.

blocks.zh: 圣经说，神的国，就在你们心里，你必须现在就活在天堂中，而不是等到死后活在天堂里面。
blocks.en: The Bible says the kingdom of God is within you. You must live in heaven now, not wait until after death to live in heaven.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 17:21
zh.text: 人也不得说，‘看哪，在这里’，‘看哪，在那里’；因为神的国就在你们心里（“心里”或作“中间”）。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 17:21
en.text: Nor will people say, "Look, here it is," or "There it is," because the kingdom of God is within you.

blocks.zh: 未来要进入的天堂对于我们来说，“好像一个物理上的存在”，现在天堂对于我们来说，“好像一种精神上的天堂”。但是义人离开后的好像一种精神上的存在，要活在一个物理意义上的天堂，听起来就很困难。
blocks.en: The heaven we will enter in the future is, for us, "like a physical reality." The heaven now is, for us, "like a spiritual heaven." But if the righteous, after leaving this world, exist as spiritual beings and have to live in a physical heaven, that sounds difficult.

blocks.zh: 如果你活在物理世界中，不能经历精神上的天堂，你死后精神上的存在就很难经历到物理意义上的天堂。当你活在物理世界上开始经历精神上的天堂，你死后精神上的存在就能够经历到物理上的天堂。
blocks.en: If you live in the physical world without experiencing the spiritual heaven, it will be hard for your spiritual existence after death to experience the physical heaven. When you begin to experience the spiritual heaven while living in the physical world, your spiritual existence after death will be able to experience the physical heaven.

blocks.zh: 实际意义上来说，天堂和将来复活的人都是跨越或超越物理世界与精神世界的存在。所以，我们在物理世界活着的时候，我们就需要活在天堂里，活在神的爱中。
blocks.en: In a real sense, heaven and those who will rise again transcend both the physical and the spiritual worlds. So while we live in the physical world, we need to live in heaven, to live in God's love.

blocks.zh: 圣经说，神就是爱，住在爱里面的就住在神的里面，神也住在爱里面的人。这样的人，在审判的时候，就不害怕地狱的火。
blocks.en: The Bible says God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God lives in the one who lives in love. Such a person will not fear the fire of hell at the judgment.

blocks.zh: 所以，现在我们就需要活在爱里面，活在基督里面，靠着基督用爱心彼此对待。当我们彼此相爱的时候，就能够叫人在理性上开始认识神。
blocks.en: So now we need to live in love, to live in Christ, and by Christ to treat one another with love. When we love one another, people can begin to know God in their understanding.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰一书 4:8
zh.text: 没有爱心的，就不认识神，因为神就是爱。

en.label: Scripture · 1 John 4:8
en.text: Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰一书 4:16
zh.text: 神爱我们的心，我们也知道、也信。神就是爱，住在爱里面的，就是住在神里面，神也住在他里面。

en.label: Scripture · 1 John 4:16
en.text: And so we know and rely on the love God has for us. God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰一书 4:17
zh.text: 这样，爱在我们里面得以完全，我们就可以在审判的日子坦然无惧。因为他如何，我们在这世上也如何。

en.label: Scripture · 1 John 4:17
en.text: This is how love is made complete among us so that we will have confidence on the day of judgment: In this world we are like Jesus.

zh.label: 圣经 · 歌罗西书 2:2
zh.text: 要叫他们的心得安慰，因爱心互相联络，以致丰丰足足在悟性中有充足的信心，使他们真知神的奥秘，就是基督。

en.label: Scripture · Colossians 2:2
en.text: My goal is that they may be encouraged in heart and united in love, so that they may have the full riches of complete understanding, in order that they may know the mystery of God, namely, Christ.

blocks.zh: 现在世界的人也会预先品尝地狱的滋味吗？
blocks.en: Do people in the world today also get a foretaste of hell?

blocks.zh: 父母精心烹饪的菜品，在很多孩子看来，不如给自己零钱去吃路边的蛋炒粉、蛋炒饭，当孩子无法感受父母的爱的时候，他想要寻找的是自己认为的自由。
blocks.en: Dishes lovingly prepared by parents, in the eyes of many children, are not as good as getting pocket money to buy fried noodles or fried rice from a street stall. When a child cannot feel the parents' love, what he seeks is the freedom he imagines.

blocks.zh: 对拒绝父母的孩子来说，他们口中的黑暗料理和父母对他们的管理，夸张点来说，他们觉得就像地狱一样。
blocks.en: For children who reject their parents, the "terrible cooking" they talk about and their parents' management of them—to put it strongly—feel like hell to them.

blocks.zh: 我们人好像是上帝的孩子，像叛逆的孩子一样，会说上帝很霸道，为什么不相信祂的人要在地狱中受苦，祂还是爱的上帝吗？
blocks.en: We human beings are like God's children. Like rebellious children, we say God is domineering: why do those who do not believe in Him suffer in hell? Is He still a God of love?

blocks.zh: 不是上帝要人在地狱中受苦，而是拒绝上帝的爱，人就很痛苦！圣经的作者只是用人能够理解的词语来形容这种没有上帝同在的光景。
blocks.en: It is not that God wants people to suffer in hell. Rather, rejecting God's love, people are in great pain! The biblical writers only used words people can understand to describe this condition of being without God.

blocks.zh: 对上帝爱的拒绝，使人仇恨上帝，拒绝爱的人在生活中的痛苦就好像在浅尝地狱的滋味一样。当我们活在仇恨中不愿意原谅、不愿意饶恕的时候，我们也很痛苦。我们苦毒不饶恕的时候，会发现身边尽都是“口臭、脸丑、踩了自己脚”的人。
blocks.en: Rejecting God's love makes people hate God. The pain in the life of one who rejects love is like a foretaste of hell. When we live in hatred, unwilling to forgive, we too are in great pain. When we are bitter and unforgiving, we find that everyone around us seems to be "bad-smelling, ugly-faced, and stepping on our feet."

blocks.zh: 当我们愿意靠近上帝的话语，活出上帝要我们的生活，我们就会开始活在神的爱里面，就好像天堂一样，而我也深信在地上活在爱中的人，将来也会活在天上神所掌权的地方，那就是充满爱的国度！阿们！
blocks.en: When we are willing to draw near to God's word and live the life God wants for us, we begin to live in God's love, like heaven itself. And I firmly believe that those who live in love on earth will one day live in the place where God reigns in heaven—a kingdom full of love! Amen!

blocks.zh: 1. 结合“叛逆孩子拒绝父母之爱”的比喻，我们该如何帮助大家理解“上帝是慈爱的，但拒绝神的人会陷入痛苦/地狱的光景”这一难题？
blocks.en: 1. Using the parable of the rebellious child rejecting his parents' love, how can we help people understand the difficulty that "God is loving, yet those who reject God fall into pain/hell"?

blocks.zh: 2. 在了解“欣嫩子谷”“塔塔鲁斯”“阴间/哈迪斯”“乐园”与“火湖”的差异后，这对你认识死后的审判与神的拯救有什么新澄清？
blocks.en: 2. After understanding the differences between the "Valley of Hinnom," "Tartarus," "Hades," "Paradise," and the "Lake of Fire," what new clarity does this bring to your understanding of judgment after death and God's salvation?

blocks.zh: 3. 耶稣说“神的国就在你们心里”，你如何在日常生活或教会彼此相爱中，真实体会神掌权的平安与天国的实际？
blocks.en: 3. Jesus said "the kingdom of God is within you." How can you truly experience the peace of God's reign and the reality of heaven in daily life or in mutual love within the church?

blocks.zh: 4. 活在仇恨和苦毒中就像“浅尝地狱的滋味”。面对关系中的伤害，我们如何靠着基督的爱迈出饶恕的第一步？
blocks.en: 4. Living in hatred and bitterness is like "a foretaste of hell." Facing hurt in relationships, how can we take the first step of forgiveness through the love of Christ?

title.en: What Does It Mean to Believe in Jesus?

verse.zh: 若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，天天背起他的十字架来跟从我<small>路加福音 9:23</small>
verse.en: If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me<small>Luke 9:23</small>

verseText.zh: 若有人要跟从我，就当舍己，天天背起他的十字架来跟从我
verseText.en: If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me

summary.zh: 从马克·吐温读《圣经》的冷幽默说起——真正困扰他的不是读不懂的地方，而是看得懂却活不出的地方。由此对比初代教会与今天信耶稣的背景差异：初代门徒信耶稣意味着把命给耶稣。再回到以色列的历史背景，从被掳归回、阿利亚行动，看宗教领袖为何逼迫耶稣，犹大的失望与出卖，提醒今天的信徒：不是环境使我们远离神，而是信仰的源头是否在耶稣基督；信耶稣关乎的不是钱，而是要不要命的问题——愿我们忠心跟随耶稣，成为结出一百倍果实的人。
summary.en: Beginning with Mark Twain's dry humor about reading the Bible—what truly troubled him was not what he could not understand, but what he understood all too well yet failed to live out. It compares the background of believing in Jesus in the early church with that of today: for the early disciples, believing in Jesus meant giving their lives to Jesus. Returning to Israel's history—from exile and return to the Aliyah—it explores why the religious leaders persecuted Jesus, and Judas's disappointment and betrayal, reminding believers today: it is not our circumstances that drive us from God, but whether the source of our faith is Jesus Christ. Believing in Jesus is not about money, but about whether we will give our lives—may we follow Jesus faithfully and become people who bear fruit a hundredfold.

blocks.zh: 一个年轻人看到马克·吐温正在读《圣经》，感到非常纳闷。在年轻人的印象中，马克·吐温总是喜欢开宗教的玩笑，甚至写过不少讽刺教会的文字。年轻人忍不住走过去问：“马克·吐温先生，您这样一位对宗教充满怀疑的人，怎么也读起《圣经》来了？难道书里那些让你想不通、读不懂的地方，让你感到困扰和焦虑吗？”
blocks.en: A young man saw Mark Twain reading the Bible and was puzzled. In the young man's impression, Mark Twain always liked to joke about religion and had even written many words satirizing the church. The young man could not help walking over and asking, “Mr. Twain, how is it that a man so skeptical of religion like you is reading the Bible? Don't the parts you can't make sense of or understand trouble and distress you?”

blocks.zh: 马克·吐温放下书，摘下眼镜，看着年轻人，用他标志性的冷幽默回答道：“小伙子，真正让我感到困扰的，并不是《圣经》里那些我‘读不懂’的地方；恰恰相反，是那些我‘完全看得懂’的地方。”
blocks.en: Mark Twain put down the book, took off his glasses, looked at the young man, and answered with his signature dry humor: “Young man, what truly troubles me is not the parts of the Bible I can't understand; on the contrary, it is the parts I understand all too well.”

blocks.zh: “If Christ were here now there is one thing he would not be a Christian.”——Mark Twain, Following the Equator (1897)
blocks.en: “If Christ were here now there is one thing he would not be a Christian.”——Mark Twain, Following the Equator (1897)

blocks.zh: 马克·吐温经常讽刺基督教徒的伪善，讽刺基督徒阅读圣经，但却没有活出圣经。不仅仅是他们那个年代如此，今天这个年代我们的基督徒也要小心：我们是不是阅读圣经，却不活出圣经。
blocks.en: Mark Twain often satirized the hypocrisy of Christians—reading the Bible yet not living it out. It was not only so in his day; Christians today must also be careful: are we reading the Bible yet not living it?

title.en: The Faith of the Early Church

blocks.zh: 我们先来看一下初代教会信耶稣的背景和今天教会信耶稣的背景比较。现在我们的决志祷告和初代教会的决志祷告其实意义上是有差异的。在初代教会，门徒们相信耶稣意味着可能会失去生命，而今天信耶稣需要付上的代价非常的小。
blocks.en: Let us first compare the background of believing in Jesus in the early church with that of the church today. Our altar-call prayer today actually differs in meaning from that of the early church. In the early church, the disciples knew that believing in Jesus could mean losing their lives, while today the cost of believing in Jesus is very small.

blocks.zh: 初代教会的门徒，他们的信仰被犹太教认为是亵渎上帝。而犹太人从摩西时期就被教导在上帝以外不可以有其他的神，而当时以色列人被引诱拜金牛犊和外邦人的其他神明，被上帝严厉的管教。
blocks.en: The faith of the early church disciples was considered blasphemy against God by Judaism. The Jews had been taught since the time of Moses that there must be no other gods besides God, and when Israel was enticed to worship the golden calf and the gods of the nations, God disciplined them severely.

blocks.zh: 后来士师时期因为一边敬拜上帝一边拜偶像，有些支派差点因此灭绝，再到后来所罗门时期以色列王朝达到鼎盛，也就在这个时期所罗门王娶一千位外邦嫔妃，并为他们建立异教神庙。以色列在所罗门之后随即分裂为南北两个国家。
blocks.en: Later, in the days of the judges, because they worshipped God on one hand and idols on the other, some tribes nearly perished. Then, in the time of Solomon, the kingdom of Israel reached its height—and it was in this period that King Solomon took one thousand foreign concubines and built pagan temples for them. After Solomon, Israel was immediately split into two kingdoms.

blocks.zh: 在南北两国期间，北国以色列基本都是拜偶像的国王，南国为大卫、所罗门王朝的正统后裔，王朝的国王有敬畏上帝的，也有随从外邦风俗敬拜偶像的。最终两个王朝先后被外邦王朝掳掠。
blocks.en: During the period of the two kingdoms, the kings of the northern kingdom of Israel were mostly idolaters, while the southern kingdom was the legitimate heir of the dynasty of David and Solomon; some of its kings feared God, while others followed foreign customs and worshipped idols. In the end, both kingdoms were conquered by foreign powers.

blocks.zh: 最后历经数百年，以色列人从外邦地陆续回归到以色列。即使在现在，以色列还是有“阿利亚行动”，就是把以色列人从各地接回到以色列。
blocks.en: Finally, over the course of hundreds of years, the people of Israel gradually returned to Israel from foreign lands. Even today, Israel still has the Aliyah, which brings Jewish people back to Israel from all over the world.

blocks.zh: 1948-1949年，受反犹浪潮与逼迫影响，约4.5万名也门犹太人卖掉家产，徒步或骑驴跨越数百英里的沙漠，前往英国控制的亚丁港（Aden）临时避难营。许多人在途中遭遇抢劫、饥饿与疾病。
blocks.en: In 1948–1949, driven by waves of anti-Semitism and persecution, about 45,000 Yemenite Jews sold their property and crossed hundreds of miles of desert on foot or by donkey to temporary refugee camps in British-controlled Aden. Many suffered robbery, hunger, and disease along the way.

blocks.zh: 1948年底，以色列联合美英飞行员及民航公司，利用近40架客机和运输机展开秘密空运。由于周边阿拉伯国家封锁领空，飞机必须冒着危险，绕道红海和危险边界航线进行长时间飞行。
blocks.en: At the end of 1948, Israel, together with American and British pilots and civilian airlines, used nearly 40 passenger and cargo planes for a secret airlift. Because the surrounding Arab states closed their airspace, the planes had to fly long, dangerous routes over the Red Sea and along hostile borders.

blocks.zh: 1948年12月-1950年9月，行动共进行了380多架次的飞行。绝大多数也门犹太人此前从未见过现代机械，他们将飞机的翅膀视为圣经预言中拯救他们的“大鹰”，安心踏上归途。
blocks.en: From December 1948 to September 1950, the operation carried out more than 380 flights. Most Yemenite Jews had never seen modern machinery; they regarded the wings of the airplanes as the “great eagle” of biblical prophecy sent to save them, and boarded them in peace.

blocks.zh: 他们在飞机上诵读出埃及记十九章4节经文，感谢上帝按照圣经的经文救他们脱离外邦人的迫害。
blocks.en: On the planes they recited Exodus 19:4, thanking God for delivering them from the persecution of the nations according to the Scriptures.

blocks.zh: 安全抵达，整个社群迁回。整场行动共计安全接回约4.9万名也门犹太人，几乎将也门几千年的犹太社群完整地接回了以色列本土。
blocks.en: They arrived safely—an entire community returned. In total, the operation safely brought back about 49,000 Yemenite Jews, nearly bringing the entire Jewish community of thousands of years in Yemen back to the land of Israel.

blocks.zh: 我们回过头来说，以色列人历史上数次被掳掠，数次归回，期间经历无数的痛苦。而这些痛苦的根源，就是因为他们离开上帝，崇拜偶像。
blocks.en: Looking back: Israel was conquered and exiled many times in history, and returned many times, experiencing countless sufferings along the way. And the root of all this suffering is that they left God and worshipped idols.

zh.label: 圣经 · 出埃及记 19:4
zh.text: 我向埃及人所行的事，你们都看见了；且看见我如鹰将你们背在翅膀上，带来归我。

en.label: Bible · Exodus 19:4
en.text: You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.

title.zh: 宗教领袖为何逼迫耶稣
title.en: Why the Religious Leaders Persecuted Jesus

blocks.zh: 所以，当三位一体的上帝，道成肉身来到这个世界，超越了以色列人的理解，而耶稣当时又有能力医病赶鬼，有极大的影响力，有极多的人跟随他。
blocks.en: So when the triune God became flesh and came into the world, beyond the understanding of Israel, Jesus also had power to heal the sick and cast out demons. He had great influence, and vast numbers followed Him.

blocks.zh: 所以当时的宗教领袖非常的担心以色列人再一次落入敬拜别神而被上帝管教的光景当中。另外一个原因，也就是以色列人的宗教领袖担心耶稣威胁到他们的统治地位。
blocks.en: The religious leaders of that time were deeply afraid that Israel would once again fall into worshipping other gods and be disciplined by God. Another reason was that the religious leaders feared Jesus threatened their position of authority.

blocks.zh: 在这些综合的因素下面，以色列人的宗教领袖，联合当时的罗马统治阶级，展开了对基督徒的逼迫，所以当时的基督徒被发现后基本上会被抓、被杀害，或者送入斗兽场。
blocks.en: Under the combination of these factors, the religious leaders of Israel joined with the Roman ruling class in persecuting Christians. Believers discovered in those days would basically be arrested, killed, or thrown into the arena.

blocks.zh: 所以我们为什么会说，初代教会他们信耶稣，跟今天的基督徒做决志祷告有一定的差异呢？因为当时他们信耶稣，基本上就是要把命给耶稣，把一切都给耶稣。相比较而言，今天做决志祷告，基督徒不必付上很大的代价。
blocks.en: So why do we say that believing in Jesus in the early church differed from today's Christians making an altar-call prayer? Because back then, believing in Jesus basically meant giving your life to Jesus—giving everything to Jesus. By comparison, today when a Christian makes an altar-call prayer, he does not have to pay much of a cost.

blocks.zh: 这也造成了当时的基督徒严格地遵守耶稣基督的教导、门徒的教导。因为他们把他们的信仰看成是比生命更重要，这一点和身处中东地区的基督徒、朝鲜的基督徒、中国文革时期的基督徒，他们的处境是类似的。
blocks.en: This is also why the early Christians strictly kept the teachings of Jesus Christ and of the apostles. They regarded their faith as more important than life itself—a situation similar to that of Christians in the Middle East, Christians in North Korea, and Christians in China during the Cultural Revolution.

blocks.zh: 今天，如果我们想要真实地跟随耶稣，做耶稣的门徒，我们就必须要回顾初代教会的历史背景，并且愿意承接这一份从使徒而来的信仰传承。
blocks.en: Today, if we truly want to follow Jesus and be His disciples, we must revisit the historical background of the early church and be willing to take up the heritage of faith passed down from the apostles.

blocks.zh: 其实耶稣的门徒犹大的信仰也是这样，当时有很多的人，包括犹大，希望耶稣是带领他们走上民族的复兴之路。
blocks.en: The faith of Jesus' disciple Judas was actually like this. Many people at that time, including Judas, hoped Jesus would lead them on the road of national restoration.

blocks.zh: 但耶稣在上十字架之前，陆续地教导门徒，自己会被抓，会受难。对犹大或者当时很多期望透过耶稣来带领以色列走上复兴之路的信徒来说，耶稣无疑是非常软弱的，不再适合他们来跟随了。
blocks.en: But before going to the cross, Jesus repeatedly taught the disciples that He would be arrested and would suffer. To Judas, and to many believers who expected Jesus to lead Israel to restoration, Jesus seemed undoubtedly too weak—no longer fit for them to follow.

blocks.zh: 所以耶稣门徒犹大对耶稣非常的失望，从而引发犹大出卖耶稣的事件。当然，这个背后也有魔鬼和撒旦的工作。我们常常说，苍蝇不叮无缝的蛋。如果不是犹大对耶稣的期望超过他对耶稣的信仰，他是不会让撒旦入了他的心、在他心中作工的。
blocks.en: So Judas was deeply disappointed with Jesus, which led to the event of Judas betraying Jesus. Of course, behind it was also the work of the devil and Satan. We often say, flies do not land on an egg with no crack. Had Judas's expectation of Jesus not exceeded his faith in Jesus, he would not have let Satan enter his heart and work within him.

blocks.zh: 今天，如果我们不是先把其他的人事物放在耶稣或者我们信仰的前面，撒旦也不能在我们心中搅扰我们的信仰。很多的时候，不是因为我们的环境使我们远离神，而是我们信仰的源头是不是耶稣基督，才导致我们是不是会被荆棘挤住。
blocks.en: Today, if we do not first put other people and things ahead of Jesus and our faith, Satan cannot disturb our faith within us. Many times it is not our circumstances that drive us away from God, but whether the source of our faith is Jesus Christ—that is what determines whether we are choked by thorns.

blocks.zh: 常常有还不信的人问，信耶稣要不要钱？涉及到钱的问题，其实不是很好回答。你问的信耶稣要不要钱？其实信耶稣关乎的是要不要命的问题。
blocks.en: People who do not yet believe often ask: does believing in Jesus cost money? Questions about money are not easy to answer. You ask whether believing in Jesus costs money; in fact, believing in Jesus is about whether you will give your life.

blocks.zh: 如果我们不愿意把我们的生命献给耶稣，在不太好的环境来临的时候，或者在信仰面对压力的时候，信仰是会被随时抛弃的。
blocks.en: If we are unwilling to offer our lives to Jesus, then when hard times come, or when our faith faces pressure, it will be cast aside at any moment.

blocks.zh: 当然，你在地上不愿意付代价来跟随神，大概有一天，耶稣来的时候，或者我们去天上的时候，我们的光景也不会太好。
blocks.en: Of course, if you are unwilling to pay the cost to follow God on earth, one day—when Jesus comes, or when we go to heaven—our condition will not be very good either.

blocks.zh: 当然，如果你在地上，用短暂的换取永恒的，你用必定会失去的换取永远不会失去的。你在天上的光景会非常的好。毕竟你在地上认耶稣，耶稣在天上也认你。
blocks.en: But if on earth you exchange the temporary for the eternal, and exchange what must be lost for what can never be lost, your condition in heaven will be very good. After all, if you acknowledge Jesus on earth, Jesus will also acknowledge you in heaven.

blocks.zh: 愿我们都能够忠心地来跟随耶稣和耶稣的话语，成为愿为耶稣付代价、收获一百倍的人。
blocks.en: May we all faithfully follow Jesus and His word, becoming people who pay the cost for Jesus and reap a hundredfold.

text.zh:
1. 结合“叛逆孩子拒绝父母之爱”的比喻，我们该如何帮助大家理解“上帝是慈爱的，但拒绝神的人会陷入痛苦/地狱的光景”这一难题？
2. 在了解“欣嫩子谷”“塔塔鲁斯”“阴间/哈迪斯”“乐园”与“火湖”的差异后，这对你认识死后的审判与神的拯救有什么新澄清？
3. 耶稣说“神的国就在你们心里”，你如何在日常生活或教会彼此相爱中，真实体会神掌权的平安与天国的实际？
4. 活在仇恨和苦毒中就像“浅尝地狱的滋味”。面对关系中的伤害，我们如何靠着基督的爱迈出饶恕的第一步？
text.en:
1. Using the parable of the rebellious child rejecting his parents' love, how can we help people understand the difficulty that "God is loving, yet those who reject God fall into pain/hell"?
2. After understanding the differences between the "Valley of Hinnom," "Tartarus," "Hades," "Paradise," and the "Lake of Fire," what new clarity does this bring to your understanding of judgment after death and God's salvation?
3. Jesus said "the kingdom of God is within you." How can you truly experience the peace of God's reign and the reality of heaven in daily life or in mutual love within the church?
4. Living in hatred and bitterness is like "a foretaste of hell." Facing hurt in relationships, how can we take the first step of forgiveness through the love of Christ?

title.zh: 耶稣两次教导彼得捕鱼
title.en: Jesus Teaches Peter to Fish Twice

verse.zh: 把船开到水深之处，下网打鱼<small>路加福音 5:4</small>
verse.en: Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch<small>Luke 5:4</small>

verseText.zh: 把船开到水深之处，下网打鱼
verseText.en: Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch

summary.zh: 从加利利海（革尼撒勒湖、提比哩亚海其实是同一片水域）的地理背景讲起，对比路加福音五章与马可福音一章对呼召的记录；默想整夜劳力一无所获的彼得，如何依然顺服把船开到水深之处，得着满网的鱼并俯伏在主面前；再看复活后的耶稣在提比哩亚海边再次教导彼得捕鱼，两次相似事件在记忆重合，门徒认出是主。最后以两个问题邀请大家一起聊聊：疲惫软弱时还愿意为耶稣撑船吗？两次捕鱼事件重合时内心感受如何？
summary.en: Beginning with the geography of the Sea of Galilee (the Lake of Gennesaret and the Sea of Tiberias are in fact the same body of water), this sermon compares the records of the call in Luke 5 and Mark 1. It meditates on Peter, who toiled all night and caught nothing, yet still obeyed, pushed out into deep water, received a net full of fish and fell at the Lord’s feet. Then we see the risen Jesus teaching Peter to fish again by the Sea of Tiberias; as the two similar events overlap in memory, the disciples recognize the Lord. Finally, two questions invite us to talk together: when you are weary and weak, are you still willing to push the boat out for Jesus? And what stirs in your heart when the two fishing events overlap in your memory?

title.en: One Body of Water, Many Names

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 5:1–2
zh.text: 耶稣站在革尼撒勒湖边，众人拥挤他，要听　神的道。他见有两只船湾在湖边，打鱼的人却离开船洗网去了。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 5:1–2
en.text: One day as Jesus was standing by the Lake of Gennesaret, the people were crowding around him and listening to the word of God. He saw at the water’s edge two boats, left there by the fishermen, who were washing their nets.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 5:3–5
zh.text: 有一只船是西门的，耶稣就上去，请他把船撑开，稍微离岸，就坐下，从船上教训众人。讲完了，对西门说：“把船开到水深之处，下网打鱼。”西门说：“夫子，我们整夜劳力，并没有打着什么。但依从你的话，我就下网。”

en.label: Scripture · Luke 5:3–5
en.text: He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to put out a little from shore. Then he sat down and taught the people from the boat. When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Put out into deep water, and let down the nets for a catch.” Simon answered, “Master, we’ve worked hard all night and haven’t caught anything. But because you say so, I will let down the nets.”

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 5:6–7
zh.text: 他们下了网，就圈住许多鱼，网险些裂开，便招呼那只船上的同伴来帮助。他们就来，把鱼装满了两只船，甚至船要沉下去。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 5:6–7
en.text: When they had done so, they caught such a large number of fish that their nets began to break. So they signaled their partners in the other boat to come and help them, and they came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 5:8–9
zh.text: 西门彼得看见，就俯伏在耶稣膝前，说：“主啊，离开我，我是个罪人！”他和一切同在的人都惊讶这一网所打的鱼。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 5:8–9
en.text: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man!” For he and all his companions were astonished at the catch of fish they had taken.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 5:10–11
zh.text: 他的伙伴西庇太的儿子雅各、约翰也是这样。耶稣对西门说：“不要怕！从今以后你要得人了。”他们把两只船拢了岸，就撇下所有的，跟从了耶稣。

en.label: Scripture · Luke 5:10–11
en.text: And so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, Simon’s partners. Then Jesus said to Simon, “Don’t be afraid; from now on you will fish for people.” So they pulled their boats up on shore, left everything and followed him.

title.zh: 呼召的另一个记录：加利利海边
title.en: Another Record of the Call: By the Sea of Galilee

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 1:16–18
zh.text: 耶稣顺着加利利的海边走，看见西门和西门的兄弟安得烈在海里撒网，他们本是打鱼的。耶稣对他们说：“来跟从我！我要叫你们得人如得鱼一样。”他们就立刻舍了网，跟从了他。

en.label: Scripture · Mark 1:16–18
en.text: As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting a net into the lake, for they were fishermen. “Come, follow me,” Jesus said, “and I will send you out to fish for people.” At once they left their nets and followed him.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 1:19–20
zh.text: 耶稣稍往前走，又见西庇太的儿子雅各和雅各的兄弟约翰在船上补网。耶稣随即招呼他们，他们就把父亲西庇太和雇工人留在船上，跟从耶稣去了。

en.label: Scripture · Mark 1:19–20
en.text: When he had gone a little farther, he saw James son of Zebedee and his brother John in a boat, preparing their nets. Without delay he called them, and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men and followed him.

title.zh: 想象力的默想：整夜劳力的彼得
title.en: A Meditation of Imagination: Peter Who Toiled All Night

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰福音 21:2–4
zh.text: 有西门彼得和称为低土马的多马，并加利利的迦拿人拿但业，还有西庇太的两个儿子，又有两个门徒，都在一处。西门彼得对他们说：“我打鱼去。”他们说：“我们也和你同去。”他们就出去，上了船，那一夜并没有打着什么。天将亮的时候，耶稣站在岸上，门徒却不知道是耶稣。

en.label: Scripture · John 21:2–4
en.text: Simon Peter, Thomas (also known as Didymus), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together. “I’m going out to fish,” Simon Peter told them, and they said, “We’ll go with you.” So they went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing. Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not realize that it was Jesus.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰福音 21:5–7
zh.text: 耶稣就对他们说：“小子，你们有吃的没有？”他们回答说：“没有。”耶稣说：“你们把网撒在船的右边，就必得着。”他们便撒下网去，竟拉不上来了，因为鱼甚多。耶稣所爱的那门徒对彼得说：“是主！”那时西门彼得赤着身子，一听见是主，就束上一件外衣，跳在海里。

en.label: Scripture · John 21:5–7
en.text: He called out to them, “Friends, haven’t you any fish?” “No,” they answered. He said, “Throw your net on the right side of the boat and you will find some.” When they did, they were unable to haul the net in because of the large number of fish. Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his outer garment around him (for he had taken it off) and jumped into the water.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰福音 21:8–9
zh.text: 其余的门徒离岸不远，约有二百肘（古代以肘为尺，一肘约有今时尺半），就在小船上把那网鱼拉过来。他们上了岸，就看见那里有炭火，上面有鱼，又有饼。

en.label: Scripture · John 21:8–9
en.text: The other disciples followed in the boat, towing the net full of fish, for they were not far from shore, about a hundred yards. When they landed, they saw a fire of burning coals there with fish on it, and some bread.

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰福音 21:10–13
zh.text: 耶稣对他们说：“把刚才打的鱼拿几条来。”西门彼得就去（或作“上船”），把网拉到岸上，那网满了大鱼，共一百五十三条。鱼虽这样多，网却没有破。耶稣说：“你们来吃早饭。”门徒中没有一个敢问他“你是谁”，因为知道是主。耶稣就来拿饼和鱼给他们。

en.label: Scripture · John 21:10–13
en.text: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.” So Simon Peter climbed back into the boat and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many the net was not torn. Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.” None of the disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Lord. Jesus came, took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.

verseText.en: Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened to you

summary.zh: 从祷告蒙垂听的喜乐与祷告无回应的无助谈起：要疏通祷告的管道——罪、疑惑、宴乐、骄傲、自义都会拦阻祷告；要有神话语的信心，信心从神的话语而来；要按神的旨意祷告；要坚持我们的祷告——寡妇和不义的官、但以理祷告二十一日、P.U.S.H.（直推到事情发生）。最后反思：祷告的管道是否畅通，是否持续等候合神心意的祷告，并相信神必垂听。
summary.en: Beginning with the joy of answered prayer and the helplessness of unanswered prayer, this sermon shows us: clear the channel of prayer—sin, doubt, pleasure, pride and self-righteousness all block prayer; have faith in God's Word, for faith comes from God's Word; pray according to God's will; and keep praying—the widow and the unjust judge, Daniel's twenty-one days of prayer, P.U.S.H. (Pray Until Something Happens). Finally it asks us to reflect: is the channel of my prayer clear, am I continuing to wait in prayer that agrees with God's will, and do I believe God will hear?
