verse.zh: 你们要饶恕人，就必蒙饶恕（“饶恕”原文作“释放”）<small>路加福音 6:37</small>
verse.en: Forgive, and you will be forgiven. (The Greek word here means “released.”)<small>Luke 6:37</small>

verseText.zh: 你们要饶恕人，就必蒙饶恕（“饶恕”原文作“释放”）
verseText.en: Forgive, and you will be forgiven. (The Greek word here means “released.”)

summary.zh: 从送孩子上学路上的一件不愉快说起，引出“饶恕”的主题：不要论断人、定人的罪，免得不饶恕论断人；不饶恕的蝴蝶效应——苦毒和仇恨会吞噬生命；饶恕到底几次？不是七次，乃是七十个七次；不止息地效法耶稣，思想国王何等大的赦免；不饶恕会让我们落在掌刑的手中，选择饶恕，才能释放自己得自由。
summary.en: Starting from an unpleasant incident on the way to send a child to school, this sermon brings up the theme of forgiveness: do not judge or condemn others, lest in refusing to forgive you judge them; the butterfly effect of unforgiveness—bitterness and hatred devour life. How many times should we forgive? Not seven times, but seventy times seven. Imitate Jesus without ceasing, and consider how great the king’s forgiveness was; unforgiveness puts us in the hands of the jailer—choose forgiveness, and you will release yourself into freedom.

blocks.zh: 这周礼拜五（2020年10月），我送加恩上学的路上，想起过去一些不愉快的事情。我就跟上帝祷告说，上帝啊，请你拿走我心中所有的恨，让我里面依然充满对你的热情；请你在我有限的爱上面施行五饼二鱼的神迹，让我能够憧憬、每一天都经历你的精彩。然后我就略加修改，放到了网上，我要表达的是，每个人的生活都可能会经历一些不愉快，但最重要的是你如何选择你的未来，这就是我们今天的主题——饶恕。
blocks.en: This past Friday (October 2020), on my way dropping Jia-En off at school, some unpleasant things from the past came to mind. I prayed to God, “Lord, please take away all the hatred in my heart, and keep it filled with passion for You; please work the miracle of the five loaves and two fish upon my limited love, so that I may look forward to and experience Your wonders every day.” I then made a few edits and posted it online. What I wanted to say is that everyone’s life may go through unpleasant times, but what matters most is how you choose your future—and that is our theme today: forgiveness.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 6:37–42
zh.text: 你们不要论断人，就不被论断；你们不要定人的罪，就不被定罪；你们要饶恕人，就必蒙饶恕（“饶恕”原文作“释放”）；你们要给人，就必有给你们的，并且用十足的升斗，连摇带按，上尖下流地倒在你们怀里；因为你们用什么量器量给人，也必用什么量器量给你们。”耶稣又用比喻对他们说：“瞎子岂能领瞎子，两个人不是都要掉在坑里吗？学生不能高过先生；凡学成了的不过和先生一样。为什么看见你弟兄眼中有刺，却不想自己眼中有梁木呢？你不见自己眼中有梁木，怎能对你弟兄说‘容我去掉你眼中的刺’呢？你这假冒为善的人！先去掉自己眼中的梁木，然后才能看得清楚，去掉你弟兄眼中的刺。

en.label: Bible · Luke 6:37–42
en.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven. Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you again. Jesus also told them this parable: “Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit? The student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher. Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye? How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”

title.zh: 不要因为不饶恕而论断人
title.en: Do Not Judge for Lack of Forgiveness

blocks.zh: 路加福音6章37节说你们不要论断人，这里论断κρίνω（音krino）的意思是，选择对别人发出批评、挑剔和谴责，来定人的罪。
blocks.en: Luke 6:37 says, do not judge. The word “judge” here, krinō (κρίνω), means choosing to criticize, find fault with, and condemn others—to pass sentence on them.

blocks.zh: 圣经不要我们去批评和论断人，但我们常常因为和他人立场不同而论断和批评、或者因为受伤的缘故内在的防卫机制影响下去论断人。但不论是什么原因我们论断人，都要想起主耶稣透过圣经对我们说的，我们不要定人的罪。
blocks.en: The Bible tells us not to criticize or judge others, yet we often judge and criticize people because we differ with them, or because our inner defense mechanisms kick in after we have been hurt. But whatever the reason we judge, we must remember what the Lord Jesus tells us through Scripture: we must not condemn others.

blocks.zh: 有些弟兄姐妹谈到哥林多前书6章3节说，岂不知我们要审判天使吗？何况今生的事呢！说到这里的审判原文和路加福音的论断是同一个字。的确是同一个字，我们理解圣经，除了参考原文字义，还需要上下文理解。
blocks.en: Some brothers and sisters point to 1 Corinthians 6:3, which asks, “Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life!” The word “judge” there is the same Greek word as “judge” in Luke. It is indeed the same word, but to understand Scripture we must look not only at the meaning of the original word but also at its context.

blocks.zh: 透过上下文，我们可以理解到，保罗说，你们可以krino，但这里的krino不是指我们主观的批评和论断，而是信徒中间有诉讼，应当交给教会，教会安排有智慧的弟兄姐妹组成团队，来帮助判断，这里有点像是教会内的审判法庭，但这里并不是指的一个权力机关，而是因为爱的缘故，来奉主的名判断弟兄与弟兄之间的问题。并且我们能够审判教内的事情，只有在一种情况下，就是弟兄与弟兄的相争，被上帝交在教会的手中的时候。教会同时也要警惕，不可以让中世纪的宗教审判之风滋长，教会是因为爱的缘故去判断，而不是主张主观的权力和辖制。
blocks.en: From the context we see that Paul is saying you may “krinō,” but here it does not mean our subjective criticism and judging. When believers have lawsuits among themselves, they should be brought to the church; the church can appoint wise brothers and sisters as a team to help discern. It is something like a judging court within the church, but not an organ of power. Rather, out of love, they judge matters between brother and brother in the name of the Lord. And we are able to judge matters within the church in only one situation: when a dispute between brothers has been entrusted by God into the church’s hands. The church must also be on guard, so that the spirit of medieval inquisition does not grow up among us. The church judges out of love, not out of a claim to subjective power and control.

blocks.zh: 那教会的审判会不会重蹈教会历史上的错误呢？如果基于彼此相爱的立场上去判断的时候，我相信不会。教会中出现诉讼的事情，教会能否作正确的审判呢？一方面，我相信当教会奉主的名去判断的时候，上帝会给与智慧和启示；另一方面，保罗甚至鼓励弟兄姐妹要情愿为主的缘故，去吃亏，而不是去欺压人、亏负人，甚至弟兄与弟兄告状，告在不信主的人面前。
blocks.en: Will the church’s judging repeat the mistakes of church history? I believe it will not, when it judges on the basis of mutual love. When lawsuits arise in the church, can the church judge rightly? On one hand, I believe that when the church judges in the Lord’s name, God gives wisdom and revelation. On the other hand, Paul even encourages brothers and sisters to be willing to suffer loss for the Lord’s sake, rather than oppressing or defrauding others—rather than one brother suing another, and doing so before unbelievers.

blocks.zh: 联系圣经的上下文，你就知道保罗不是说我们可以随主观想法去论断人的，不管是我们有一颗熊熊燃烧的八卦之心，还是我觉得内心受到打击和创伤，我们都不可以去私下的论断人，而是被教会托付公开的去判断教会内弟兄相争的事情。
blocks.en: Read in its biblical context, you see that Paul is not saying we may judge people according to our own subjective ideas. Whether we burn with gossipy curiosity, or feel ourselves deeply wounded and hurt, we must not judge people privately; rather, we are publicly entrusted by the church to judge disputes between brothers within the church.

blocks.zh: 我们继续回到路加福音6章来看，在“你们不要论断人……你们不要定人的罪……”的“你们”之前含有一个语助词，没有被翻译出来，καί（音kai）意思有即使是事实，我们也不要论断。我们有两个方面需要注意，一、我们所知道的有限，我们可以出现主观的臆测，即我们所判断的可能不正确；二、我们所判断的即或正确，神也不要我们论断，除非是按圣经所说，由于弟兄姐妹彼此亏负，交托给教会来审断的事件。
blocks.en: Returning to Luke 6, note that before the “you” in “do not judge… do not condemn…” there is a particle, kai (καί, pronounced “kai”), that has not been translated; it implies: even if it is a fact, we still must not judge. Two things stand out. First, our knowledge is limited; we may offer subjective guesses, and what we judge may be wrong. Second, even if what we judge is correct, God does not want us to judge—unless, as Scripture says, brothers and sisters have wronged one another and the matter has been entrusted to the church for judgment.

zh.label: 圣经 · 哥林多前书 6:1–8
zh.text: 你们中间有彼此相争的事，怎敢在不义的人面前求审，不在圣徒面前求审呢？岂不知圣徒要审判世界吗？若世界为你们所审，难道你们不配审判这最小的事吗？岂不知我们要审判天使吗？何况今生的事呢！既是这样，你们若有今生的事当审判，是派教会所轻看的人审判吗？我说这话是要叫你们羞耻。难道你们中间没有一个智慧人能审断弟兄们的事吗？你们竟是弟兄与弟兄告状，而且告在不信主的人面前。你们彼此告状，这已经是你们的大错了。为什么不情愿受欺呢？为什么不情愿吃亏呢？你们倒是欺压人、亏负人，况且所欺压、所亏负的就是弟兄！

en.label: Bible · 1 Corinthians 6:1–8
en.text: If any of you has a dispute with another, do you dare to take it to court before the unrighteous, instead of taking it to the saints? Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if you are to judge the world, are you not competent to judge trivial cases? Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the things of this life! Therefore, if you have disputes about such matters, do you ask for a ruling from those whose way of life is scorned in the church? I say this to shame you. Is it possible that there is nobody among you wise enough to judge a dispute between believers? But instead, one brother takes another to court—and this in front of unbelievers! The very fact that you have lawsuits among you means you have been completely defeated already. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be cheated? Instead, you yourselves cheat and do wrong, and you do this to your brothers and sisters.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 6:37–42
zh.text: 你们不要论断人，就不被论断；你们不要定人的罪，就不被定罪；你们要饶恕人，就必蒙饶恕（“饶恕”原文作“释放”）；你们要给人，就必有给你们的，并且用十足的升斗，连摇带按，上尖下流地倒在你们怀里；因为你们用什么量器量给人，也必用什么量器量给你们。”耶稣又用比喻对他们说：“瞎子岂能领瞎子，两个人不是都要掉在坑里吗？学生不能高过先生；凡学成了的不过和先生一样。为什么看见你弟兄眼中有刺，却不想自己眼中有梁木呢？你不见自己眼中有梁木，怎能对你弟兄说‘容我去掉你眼中的刺’呢？你这假冒为善的人！先去掉自己眼中的梁木，然后才能看得清楚，去掉你弟兄眼中的刺。

en.label: Bible · Luke 6:37–42
en.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven. Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you again. Jesus also told them this parable: “Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into a pit? The student is not above the teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like their teacher. Why do you look at the speck of sawdust in your brother’s eye and pay no attention to the plank in your own eye? How can you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you yourself fail to see the plank in your own eye? You hypocrite, first take the plank out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.”

blocks.zh: 圣经要我们“不要论断人、定人的罪，这样我们就不被论断、不被定罪”。这里不是不被人论断，而是不被上帝审判和定罪。当我们被人伤害的时候，我们选择饶恕，我们就在上帝面前，从伤害里面得着释放和自由。而当我们不饶恕的时候，一方面，我们的心灵仍然处在囚牢当中，耿耿于怀；另一方面，不饶恕和苦毒的心也会滋生生理上的毒气来残害我们的身体。
blocks.en: Scripture tells us “do not judge or condemn others, so that you will not be judged or condemned.” This does not mean not being judged by people, but not being judged and condemned by God. When we are hurt by others, choosing forgiveness means that before God we find release and freedom from that hurt. When we do not forgive, on one hand our soul stays in prison, clinging to the grievance; on the other hand, an unforgiving and bitter heart also breeds spiritual poison that destroys our bodies.

blocks.zh: 并且圣经说，你们要给人，就必有给你们的，并且用十足的升斗，连摇带按，上尖下流地倒在你们怀里；因为你们用什么量器量给人，也必用什么量器量给你们。过去你可能听过教会要我们奉献得时候，讲解这节经文。但这里得经文其实和饶恕有关。因为我们不饶恕，我们不饶恕得后果就会像升斗一样连摇带按的还给我们，这也是为什么苦毒和仇恨会吞噬我们的缘故了。
blocks.en: Scripture also says, “Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together and running over, will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured to you again.” You may have heard this verse preached when the church asks us to give offerings, but this verse is actually about forgiveness. Because we do not forgive, the consequences of our unforgiveness are measured back to us, pressed down and shaken together—this is why bitterness and hatred consume us.

blocks.zh: 可以说，不饶恕使得我们的身体都被过去的创伤摧残。饶恕就是选择让上帝来申冤报仇，对于我们来说就是选择放手、不再仇恨，让自己得自由。被苦毒辖制引起的身心的痛苦，选择饶恕，就是选择得医治。饶恕之前我们是瞎眼得，饶恕之后，我们就是瞎眼的重见光明。
blocks.en: It can be said that unforgiveness leaves our bodies ravaged by past wounds. Forgiveness is choosing to let God repay justice; for us it means letting go, no longer hating, and setting ourselves free. In the body and soul pain caused by bitterness, choosing forgiveness is choosing healing. Before forgiveness we were blind; after forgiveness, the blind receive their sight.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 17:1–4
zh.text: 耶稣又对门徒说：“绊倒人的事是免不了的，但那绊倒人的有祸了。就是把磨石拴在这人的颈项上，丢在海里，还强如他把这小子里的一个绊倒了。你们要谨慎！“若是你的弟兄得罪你，就劝戒他；他若懊悔，就饶恕他。倘若他一天七次得罪你，又七次回转，说：‘我懊悔了’，你总要饶恕他。”

en.label: Bible · Luke 17:1–4
en.text: Jesus said to his disciples: “Things that cause people to stumble are bound to come, but woe to anyone through whom they come. It would be better for them to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck than to cause one of these little ones to stumble. So watch yourselves. If your brother or sister sins against you, rebuke them; and if they repent, forgive them. Even if they sin against you seven times in a day and seven times come back to you saying ‘I repent,’ you must forgive them.”

title.en: How Many Times Must We Forgive?

blocks.zh: 我们到底要饶恕人几次呢？耶稣教导说，如果有一个人得罪你，要劝诫他，如果他后悔，你就饶恕他。如果他一天七次得罪你，又七次道歉回转，说，我后悔了。你总要饶恕他。耶稣在这里说的及时的悔改和及时的饶恕，不可含怒到日落。
blocks.en: How many times must we forgive? Jesus teaches that if someone sins against you, rebuke them; if they repent, forgive them. If they sin against you seven times in a day and seven times turn back, saying, “I repent,” you must forgive them. What Jesus speaks of here is timely repentance and timely forgiveness; do not let the sun go down while you are still angry.

zh.label: 圣经 · 以弗所书 4:26
zh.text: 生气却不要犯罪，不可含怒到日落…

en.label: Bible · Ephesians 4:26
en.text: “In your anger do not sin”: Do not let the sun go down while you are still angry…

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 18:21–35
zh.text: 那时，彼得进前来，对耶稣说：“主啊，我弟兄得罪我，我当饶恕他几次呢？到七次可以吗？”耶稣说：“我对你说，不是到七次，乃是到七十个七次。天国好像一个王要和他仆人算账。才算的时候，有人带了一个欠一千万银子的来。因为他没有什么偿还之物，主人吩咐把他和他妻子儿女，并一切所有的都卖了偿还。那仆人就俯伏拜他，说：‘主啊，宽容我！将来我都要还清。’那仆人的主人就动了慈心，把他释放了，并且免了他的债。那仆人出来，遇见他的一个同伴欠他十两银子，便揪着他，掐住他的喉咙，说：‘你把所欠的还我！’他的同伴就俯伏央求他说：‘宽容我吧！将来我必还清。’他不肯，竟去把他下在监里，等他还了所欠的债。众同伴看见他所作的事，就甚忧愁，去把这事都告诉了主人。于是，主人叫了他来，对他说：‘你这恶奴才！你央求我，我就把你所欠的都免了。你不应当怜恤你的同伴，像我怜恤你吗？’主人就大怒，把他交给掌刑的，等他还清了所欠的债。你们各人若不从心里饶恕你的弟兄，我天父也要这样待你们了。”

en.label: Bible · Matthew 18:21–35
en.text: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Up to seven times?” Jesus answered, “I tell you, not seven times, but seventy-seven times. Therefore, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants. As he began the settlement, a man who owed him ten thousand bags of gold was brought to him. Since he was not able to pay, the master ordered that he and his wife and his children and all that he had be sold to repay the debt. At this the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Be patient with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’ The servant’s master took pity on him, canceled the debt and let him go. But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred silver coins. He grabbed him and began to choke him. ‘Pay back what you owe me!’ he demanded. His fellow servant fell to his knees and begged him, ‘Be patient with me, and I will pay you back.’ But he refused. Instead, he went off and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay the debt. When the other servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed and went and told their master everything that had happened. Then the master called the servant in. ‘You wicked servant,’ he said, ‘I canceled all that debt of yours because you begged me to. Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?’ In anger his master handed him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should pay back all he owed. This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart.”

blocks.zh: 耶稣教导门徒弟兄得罪自己悔改后要一天饶恕七次，彼得就对耶稣说，我饶恕我弟兄七次可以吗？我想如果我们代入彼得的角色，不难发现其实彼得觉得自己做的很棒了，其实是的，彼得已经做的好棒了，比我们大部分人都棒了。但耶稣不是要我们自己的努力行律法的样子，耶稣要我们思想祂为我们所成就的。祂的十字架，不是对我们一次次的饶恕吗？当我们思想祂对我们今生无限的赦免，我们才能饶恕人七十个七次！不停止的去效法耶稣基督。
blocks.en: Jesus taught that when a brother sins against you and repents, you must forgive him seven times a day. So Peter asked Jesus, “Shall I forgive my brother seven times?” If we put ourselves in Peter’s place, it is easy to see that Peter felt he was doing quite well—and indeed he was. Peter was doing wonderfully, better than most of us. But Jesus does not want us to rely on our own effort to keep the law; he wants us to consider what he has accomplished for us. His cross—was that not forgiveness toward us, again and again? When we consider his boundless forgiveness toward us in this life, only then can we forgive others seventy-seven times! Imitating Jesus Christ without ceasing.

title.zh: 国王的赦免是何等的大

blocks.zh: 耶稣说，有一个人欠天国国王一千万银子，无法偿还，天国的王就派人去变卖这个欠债的人所有的，他的妻子儿女，但是因为这个欠债的人，请求国王的宽容。国王心存怜悯就免了他的债。但是他遇到欠他十两银子的朋友，却不愿意宽容自己的朋友，把自己的朋友下在监狱当中，国王知道以后很生气！就对他说，“你这恶奴才！你央求我，我就把你所欠的都免了。你不应当怜恤你的同伴，像我怜恤你吗？”就把他交给掌刑的，等他还清了所欠的债。
blocks.en: Jesus tells of a man who owed the king of the kingdom of heaven ten thousand talents and could not repay. The king ordered that this debtor, his wife and children, and all he had be sold to repay. But because the debtor begged the king for mercy, the king, filled with compassion, canceled his debt. Yet when that man met a friend who owed him a hundred denarii, he would not forgive his friend, but had him thrown into prison. When the king learned of this, he was very angry and said to him, “You wicked servant! I canceled all that debt of yours because you begged me. Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant just as I had on you?” And he handed him over to the jailers until he should pay back all he owed.

blocks.zh: 这个欠债的人就是我们，耶稣在十字架上，为我们的罪，我们所有的不完全，牺牲自己，使我们能够因为信靠祂有全新的生命。但我们时常恨得罪我们的人。我们不就是那忘记自己曾经是上帝赦免的人吗？耶稣为我们所牺牲的，比起人我们的得罪和伤害来说，耶稣的牺牲是何等的大！
blocks.en: That debtor is us. On the cross Jesus sacrificed himself for our sins, for all our incompleteness, so that through trusting in him we might have new life. Yet we often hate those who sin against us. Are we not exactly the people who have forgotten that we ourselves were once forgiven by God? Compared with the wrongs and hurts others have done to us, how great is the sacrifice of Jesus!

title.zh: 不饶恕让我们落在掌刑的手中
title.en: Unforgiveness Hands Us to the Jailers

blocks.zh: 而34节告诉我们，不饶恕会使我们落入掌刑的手中，这掌刑的就是魔鬼。我们的不饶恕会使我们落入魔鬼的手中受折磨，使我们的身体和心灵被不断的煎熬。不是魔鬼有什么大的能力和权柄，而是我们的不饶恕，给与魔鬼权柄来伤害我们。只等我们选择饶恕并依靠耶稣十字架的大能，使我们脱离魔鬼权势的辖制。
blocks.en: Verse 34 tells us that unforgiveness hands us over to the jailers—and these jailers are the devil. Our unforgiveness hands us into the devil’s hands to be tormented, so that body and soul are constantly racked. It is not that the devil has some great power or authority; rather, our unforgiveness gives the devil authority to harm us. Only when we choose forgiveness and rely on the power of the cross of Jesus are we freed from the dominion of the devil’s power.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 18:34–35
zh.text: 主人就大怒，把他交给掌刑的，等他还清了所欠的债。你们各人若不从心里饶恕你的弟兄，我天父也要这样待你们了。

en.label: Bible · Matthew 18:34–35
en.text: In anger his master handed him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should pay back all he owed. This is how my heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother or sister from your heart.

title.zh: 选择饶恕释放自己得自由

blocks.zh: 在饶恕之后，我们心中的捆绑和折磨的绳索就不再紧紧勒住我们，使我们能够靠着耶稣得胜，当我们选择让耶稣的十字架来医治我们的时候，我们的绳索就要完全脱落了！
blocks.en: After forgiveness, the cords that bind and torment us no longer strangle us tightly, and we can overcome through Jesus. When we choose to let the cross of Jesus heal us, our ropes fall completely away!

blocks.zh:
我得罪了谁？谁又得罪了我？
我又要饶恕谁？
blocks.en:
Whom have I wronged? Who has wronged me?
Whom do I need to forgive?

verse.zh: 因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治<small>彼得前书 2:24</small>
verse.en: By his wounds you have been healed<small>1 Peter 2:24</small>

verseText.zh: 因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治
verseText.en: By his wounds you have been healed

summary.zh: 讲员先分享自己亲身经历神医治的经验，再谈到医治是教会的 DNA——凡来到我们中间的病人都要得到医治。相信是有力量的：要相信圣经关于医治和释放的应许；你若信，就必看见神的荣耀，信是得着，就必得着。也揭示疾病出于灵性空间的盗贼，最后以决志祷告呼召回应。
summary.en: The speaker first shares his own firsthand experience of God’s healing, then shows that healing is the DNA of the church—every sick person who comes among us should be healed. Faith is powerful: believe the Bible’s promises about healing and deliverance; if you believe, you will see the glory of God, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours. It also reveals that disease comes from the thief in the spiritual realm, and closes with an altar call of decision prayer.

title.zh: 我自己经历到神医治的经验
title.en: My Own Experience of God’s Healing

zh.label: 圣经 · 彼得前书 2:24
zh.text: 他被挂在木头上，亲身担当了我们的罪，使我们既然在罪上死，就得以在义上活。因他受的鞭伤，你们便得了医治。

en.label: Scripture · 1 Peter 2:24
en.text: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed.

title.zh: 你若信，就必看见神的荣耀
title.en: If You Believe, You Will See the Glory of God

zh.label: 圣经 · 约翰福音 11:40
zh.text: 耶稣说：“我不是对你说过，你若信，就必看见　神的荣耀吗？”

en.label: Scripture · John 11:40
en.text: Then Jesus said, “Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?”

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 11:24

summary.zh: 从衡阳 2018 年 4 月禁食祷告会的医治见证开始，分享见证如何点燃人的渴慕、见证是我们的产业；相信神要医治这个破碎的世代，我们欠这个世代一个遇见神大能的机会。神的灵带下神的能力，说方言造就自己；并从教会复兴历史中的医治特会，看见神透过医治带出复兴的心意。
summary.en: Beginning with a healing testimony from a fast-and-prayer gathering in Hengyang in April 2018, this sermon shares how testimonies kindle our longing and how testimony is our inheritance. It believes God wants to heal this broken generation, and that we owe this generation a chance to encounter God’s power. The Spirit of God brings God’s power, and speaking in tongues edifies; through healing conferences in the history of church revival, we see God’s heart to bring revival through healing.

title.zh: 为什么每次聚会，都先分享见证？
title.en: Why do we always share testimonies first in every gathering?

blocks.zh: 2018年4月2号，叶老师和我在衡阳带领禁食祷告会。当天我开始带祷告会以先，叶老师已经把整个会场的属灵气氛带的很棒了，弟兄姐妹都很热切的祷告寻求神。我分享了我们教会3月半通宵祷告弟兄姐妹的见证：“有人在渴慕时，被圣灵充满”；“有人分享圣灵带领她看到主耶稣，并鼓励她勇敢的走向主耶稣”；以及在3月的某个晨更祷告会上，一位姐妹跳起了灵舞赞美神。衡阳的弟兄姐妹就非常渴慕，在祷告会中遇见神和神大能的运行。
blocks.en: On April 2, 2018, Teacher Ye and I led a fasting prayer meeting in Hengyang. Before I began that afternoon, Teacher Ye had already built a wonderful spiritual atmosphere in the whole room, and the brothers and sisters were earnestly praying and seeking God. I shared testimonies from our church’s half-night prayer in March: “someone was filled with the Holy Spirit as they hungered”; “someone shared that the Holy Spirit led her to see the Lord Jesus and encouraged her to walk boldly toward Him”; and at one early-morning prayer meeting in March, a sister danced in the Spirit to praise God. The brothers and sisters in Hengyang hungered greatly and met God and the working of His great power in the prayer meeting.

blocks.zh: 这次聚会的神迹和医治，因为主耶稣的怜悯和爱，另外和弟兄姐妹的渴慕也是分不开的。整个会场的弟兄姐妹很渴慕，也很热切的寻求。另一方面，中场见证的时候，彼此的见证鼓励弟兄姐妹进入更深切的渴慕当中，以至于更多的人被圣灵触摸，倒在圣灵里面。极大的敬畏之情在会场中涌流，为罪、为义痛哭流涕的呼求与圣灵中的喜乐在整个会场，还有一个服侍的同工领受了圣灵如火的充满，非常的强烈。
blocks.en: The miracles and healings in this gathering came through the Lord Jesus’s mercy and love, and were also inseparable from the hunger of the brothers and sisters. The whole room hungered and sought earnestly. Moreover, as testimonies were shared midway, they encouraged one another into deeper hunger, so that more people were touched by the Holy Spirit and fell under the Spirit. A great awe swept through the room—crying out over sin and righteousness, and joy in the Holy Spirit filled the whole place; one serving co-worker also received a very strong, fiery filling of the Holy Spirit.

blocks.zh: 也就是说，见证会成为我们的产业。圣经中约书亚记24:31，约书亚在世和约书亚死后，那些知道耶和华为以色列人所行诸事的长老还在的时候，以色列人事奉耶和华。而在士师记时期，失去传承神的见证的年代，圣经形容士师记21:25：“那时以色列中没有王，各人任意而行。”我知道大部分人会把家产留给自己的后代，但你没有想过，见证是你的产业呢？出埃及那些经历神超自然大能的以色列人，后代不记得神的作为的时候，就任意妄为。你要不要做见证，让见证成为你的产业呢？
blocks.en: In other words, testimony becomes our inheritance. In Joshua 24:31, Israel served the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and all the days of the elders who outlived him, who had known all the works the Lord had done for Israel. But in the days of the judges, when testimony of God was no longer passed on, Scripture describes Judges 21:25: “in those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit.” I know most people leave their estate to their descendants, but have you never considered that testimony is your inheritance? The Israelites who experienced God’s supernatural power at the Exodus—when their descendants no longer remembered God’s deeds, they acted wickedly. Will you not give a testimony, that testimony may become your inheritance?

blocks.zh: 我要告诉你，我不仅要作见证，而且，我还会详细的告诉我的后代，我是怎样认识耶稣，是怎样经历耶稣的。我一定要把这个属灵的产业，传递给自己的后裔。所以，我也同样鼓励你：见证是你的产业，而见证的时候，是有耶稣预言的灵，听到的人就能领受到神的大能，以及带来医治和释放。
blocks.en: I want to tell you: I will not only give a testimony, I will also tell my descendants in detail how I came to know Jesus and how I have experienced Him. I must pass on this spiritual inheritance to my descendants. So I likewise encourage you: testimony is your inheritance, and when you testify, the Spirit of prophecy is present, so that those who hear receive the power of God, and healing and deliverance come.

blocks.zh: 所以我们需要做见证。见证就好像被公证员见证光明国度和黑暗国度的纠纷一样，而当公证员说，这个医治是因为耶稣已经为你付上代价，是属于你的。这个见证就好像公证员公证过的作用，然后你就比较容易持守你的医治。我知道很多人不愿意做见证，因为我们大部分有一种习惯叫做含蓄，比较不愿在人前表达自己。而你要知道见证是你的产业，在启示录12:11：“弟兄胜过它，是因羔羊的血和自己所见证的道……”当你开始做见证，你就能够依靠见证中羔羊宝血的大能胜过魔鬼。魔鬼就不容易偷窃你的医治了，因为已经被公证过了。而有些人常常在医治聚会中得着医治，过了半年左右疾病又反复，而启示录中的经文告诉我们，见证激发的祝福和能力就能够胜过魔鬼的作为。
blocks.en: So we need to testify. Testimony is like a notary witnessing the dispute between the kingdom of light and the kingdom of darkness; and when the notary declares that this healing belongs to you because Jesus has already paid the price, the testimony has the force of a notarized deed, and it becomes easier to hold fast to your healing. I know many people are unwilling to testify, because most of us have a habit called reserve—we are reluctant to express ourselves before others. But you must know that testimony is your inheritance. In Revelation 12:11: “they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony…” When you begin to testify, you can overcome the devil through the power of the blood of the Lamb in your testimony. The devil can no longer steal your healing so easily, because it has been notarized. Some people often receive healing at healing meetings, then about half a year later the illness returns; but the verse in Revelation tells us that the blessing and power stirred up by testimony can overcome the works of the devil.

blocks.zh: 巽光牧师在18年2月的天国文化的特会上分享：“在伯特利教会所在的雷丁市，有一个敞开的天，在这个城市更容易经历神。”这个虽然在非常偏远、不到十万人城市的伯特利教会，而他们是如何影响跟震动全世界，不但每年吸引了两千五百个学生，携家带眷的来到这个地方受装备，也送出了成千上万的复兴家，不断地在震动列国。（参考asia for jesus的官网介绍）。而我相信神的心意是，神迹奇事不应该成为偶发的事件而已，应该成为基督徒最自然的经历。我相信神渴望透过医治释放，彰显祂无限的怜悯，以及彰显神渴望在全地带下复兴的心意！
blocks.en: Pastor Xun Guang shared at a Heavenly Culture conference in February 2018: “Over the city of Reading, where Bethel Church is, there is an open heaven; it is easier to experience God in that city.” Though Bethel Church is in a very remote city of fewer than a hundred thousand people, how has it influenced and shaken the whole world? It not only draws twenty-five hundred students every year, coming with their whole families to be equipped, but also sends out tens of thousands of revivalists who continually shake the nations (see the Asia for Jesus website). And I believe God’s heart is that signs and wonders should not be rare accidents, but the most natural experience of a Christian. I believe God longs, through healing and deliverance, to reveal His boundless mercy and to reveal His heart to bring revival to the whole earth!

blocks.zh: 我呼吁更多青年弟兄姐妹去渴慕进到圣灵里面，更深的渴慕神的圣灵，去追求神透过圣灵来复兴我们。使我们能够进入其中，并开始看见神大能的作为成为我们教会普遍的经历。并且能够激发更多的人去寻求神，追求属灵的奋兴，进入神大能的同在中；使我们不仅经历神，也带领人进入神的大能中。
blocks.en: I call on more young brothers and sisters to hunger to enter into the Holy Spirit, to hunger more deeply for God’s Spirit, and to seek that God would revive us through the Spirit—so that we may enter in and begin to see the mighty works of God become the common experience of our church; and so that we may stir up more people to seek God, to pursue spiritual revival, and to enter the mighty presence of God—so that we not only experience God ourselves, but also lead others into God’s power.

zh.label: 圣经 · 诗篇 119:111
zh.text: 我以永远的法度（英文是见证），为永远的产业，因这是我心中所喜爱的。

en.label: Bible · Psalm 119:111
en.text: Your statutes are my heritage forever; they are the joy of my heart.

title.zh: 相信神要医治这个破碎的世代
title.en: God wants to heal this broken generation

blocks.zh: 一直以来我非常的相信神的心意要医治这个破碎的世代，无论是身体的疾病得医治；还是内心的创伤得医治。我相信这是神对教会的呼召：你们去传天国的福音，医治病人，把鬼赶出去！我相信神全备的福音应当包含医治。而神超自然的医治能够启动人心对上帝的渴慕与顺从。当人开始遇到上帝的大能，降服下来，就没有那么困难了！现在我也还是非常期盼神在每一次聚会中，不断的彰显祂大能同在！
blocks.en: All along I have deeply believed that it is God’s heart to heal this broken generation—whether the healing of physical sickness or the healing of inner wounds. I believe this is God’s call to the church: “Go, preach the gospel of the kingdom, heal the sick, drive out demons!” I believe God’s full gospel must include healing. And God’s supernatural healing can awaken a person’s hunger and obedience toward God. Once a person encounters God’s power and bows down, it is no longer so hard. Even now I greatly long that God would continually reveal His mighty presence in every gathering!

blocks.zh: 然而，我也相信神的心意，不仅仅是医治而已，更是渴望透过医治释放，点燃我们里面复兴的火焰，去为耶稣基督燃烧我们的生命，让基督的真光，照耀在这个世界。照亮死荫幽谷中的人，让人们看见神的大能，启动里面的复兴！让全地看见神的荣耀！
blocks.en: Yet I also believe God’s heart is not only healing; He longs, through healing and deliverance, to kindle the flame of revival within us, to burn our lives for Jesus Christ, and to let the true light of Christ shine into this world—to shine on those in the valley of the shadow of death, that people may see God’s power and awaken the revival within! Let the whole earth see the glory of God!

title.zh: 欠这个世代遇见神大能的机会
title.en: We owe this generation a chance to meet God’s power

blocks.zh: 圣经说的是信的人必有神迹随着他们，奉耶稣基督的名赶鬼，说新方言，手按病人，病人得医治，没有说只有特定的人。所以，你要知道，我们这些信的人，应该去彰显神医治的能力。我很喜欢比尔强生牧师说的一句话：我们欠这个世代一次遇见神的机会。你若能够领受，就应该把神的话语铭刻在内心，你里面有神预留的医治大能！而你需要相信并领受，并且凭着相信去为病人祷告！
blocks.en: The Scripture says that signs will accompany those who believe—driving out demons in the name of Jesus Christ, speaking in new tongues, laying hands on the sick that they may be healed—it does not say only certain people. So you must know that we who believe should reveal the healing power of God. I love a saying of Pastor Bill Johnson: we owe this generation an encounter with God. If you can receive it, you should engrave the word of God on your heart—the healing power God has reserved is within you! And you need to believe and receive, and by faith pray for the sick!

blocks.zh: 所以，你不止是要渴望领受从神而来的医治；也要渴望复兴的火点燃你的生命。去活出神要你活出的生命光景。
blocks.en: So you must not only long to receive healing from God; you must also long for the fire of revival to kindle your life, and live out the life that God calls you to live.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 16:16–18
zh.text: 信而受洗的，必然得救；不信的，必被定罪。信的人必有神迹随着他们：就是奉我的名赶鬼，说新方言，手能拿蛇，若喝了什么毒物，也必不受害，手按病人，病人就必好了。

en.label: Bible · Mark 16:16–18
en.text: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up snakes with their hands; and when they drink deadly poison, it will not hurt them at all; they will place their hands on sick people, and they will get well.

title.en: The Spirit of God brings the power of God

blocks.zh: 从这两节经文的对比，你可以看到，神的灵是带着神的能力的！而你需要神的圣灵不断的充满你，以至于你里面有充足的神的大能，去为耶稣基督去服侍上帝放在你身边的人。
blocks.en: From the contrast between these two verses you can see that the Spirit of God carries the power of God! And you need the Holy Spirit to fill you continually, so that there is within you an ample supply of God’s mighty power to serve, for the sake of Jesus Christ, the people God places around you.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 12:28
zh.text: 我若靠着神的灵赶鬼，这就是神的国临到你们了。

en.label: Bible · Matthew 12:28
en.text: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

zh.label: 圣经 · 路加福音 11:20
zh.text: 我若靠着神的能力赶鬼，这就是神的国临到你们了。

en.label: Bible · Luke 11:20
en.text: But if it is by the finger of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

title.en: Speaking in tongues builds up yourself

blocks.zh: 神的灵会带下神的能力，而说方言是神透过奥秘的方式在灵里面来造就自己，是需要信心来启动这种造就的，因为你的悟性是听不懂方言说什么。人们做自己不明白或没有把握的事情，都是需要信心。而这种信心就能够启动方言恩赐在灵里面造就的功效。并且也正是信心让你得着神的能力。
blocks.en: The Spirit of God brings the power of God, and speaking in tongues is God building you up in your spirit through a mysterious way. This building up needs faith to set it in motion, because your mind cannot understand what the tongues are saying. People need faith whenever they do something they do not fully understand or are not sure about. And this faith sets in motion the effect of the gift of tongues building you up in the spirit. It is also faith that lets you receive the power of God.

blocks.zh: 说方言是圣灵充满其中一个记号。在圣灵充满和说方言中，能够带下神的同在。我们每个人都有耶稣所给予的能力，而区别是有人活出来了，有人没有活出来。说方言是用隐秘的话语造就自己，让自己里面神的能力能够彰显出来。说方言就好像用水泵抽水一样，一次次的按压式的方言，看起来单调重复，却会从内心井中打出活水的泉源，带下生命的能力。
blocks.en: Speaking in tongues is one of the signs of being filled with the Holy Spirit. In being filled with the Spirit and speaking in tongues, the presence of God is brought down. Each of us has the ability Jesus gave; the difference is that some live it out and some do not. Speaking in tongues builds you up with secret words, letting the power of God within you be revealed. Speaking in tongues is like drawing water with a pump—pressing it again and again may seem monotonous and repetitive, yet it draws up from the inner well a spring of living water, bringing the power of life.

zh.label: 圣经 · 哥林多前书 14:4
zh.text: 说方言的，是造就自己。

en.label: Bible · 1 Corinthians 14:4
en.text: Anyone who speaks in a tongue edifies themselves.

zh.label: 圣经 · 哥林多前书 14:2
zh.text: 那说方言的，原不是对人说，乃是对神说，因为没有人听出来。然而他在心灵里，却是讲说各样的奥秘。

en.label: Bible · 1 Corinthians 14:2
en.text: For anyone who speaks in a tongue does not speak to people but to God. Indeed, no one understands them; they utter mysteries by the Spirit.

zh.label: 圣经 · 哥林多前书 14:14
zh.text: 我若用方言祷告，是我的灵祷告，但我的悟性没有果效。

en.label: Bible · 1 Corinthians 14:14
en.text: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is fruitless.

blocks.zh: 圣经中，耶稣走到哪里都有医治。教会历史上的复兴，都伴随着医治特会和神迹的超自然彰显。包括宗教改革的约翰卫斯理、怀特腓尔德，以及芬尼、慕迪、凯莉蒙哥马利、约翰雷克等等，这些教会历史上带领复兴聚会的弟兄姐妹，他们的聚会都是充满超自然的医治释放和圣灵充满、圣灵击倒、魂游象外等等。当然很多书籍没有记载他们聚会的场面，只记载了他们讲道的文章及他们个人传记，只是删除了圣灵外显的作为，只因为这些作者不认同圣灵的外在彰显是复兴的源头。
blocks.en: In the Bible, wherever Jesus went there was healing. Revivals in church history were always accompanied by healing conferences and the supernatural manifestation of signs and wonders—including John Wesley and George Whitefield of the Reformation, as well as Finney, Moody, Kathryn Kuhlman, John Lake, and others. The gatherings of those who led revival in church history were full of supernatural healing and deliverance, being filled with the Holy Spirit, slain in the Spirit, and being carried away in the Spirit. Of course, many books do not record the scenes of their gatherings; they record only their sermons and biographies, deleting the outward works of the Spirit, simply because those authors did not recognize the outward manifestation of the Spirit as the source of revival.

blocks.zh: 有一本教会复兴历史的书籍，里面记载一位复兴的点火者叫约翰雷克，他说过这样一句话：“我相信我是有史以来最渴慕神的人。”他要追求的是“更多”，而不是聚会结束时的一个有趣经历。他渴望活出第一世纪使徒们的生活样式，渴望到都会心痛。
blocks.en: There is a book on the history of church revival that tells of an igniter of revival named John Lake. He said, “I believe I am the person who has hungered most for God in all history.” What he pursued was “more,” not merely an interesting experience when the meeting ended. He longed to live out the way of life of the apostles of the first century—a longing so deep it ached.

blocks.zh: 1908年非洲第一场聚会，雷克祈求释放圣灵到五百多名祖鲁族人身上，复兴立刻爆发。在南非讲道时，有一个人干扰聚会，雷克用手指着他说“坐下来”，那人好像被击倒一样，跌在地上一躺三个小时。恢复过来后他说：“有东西打到我，穿过我的身体，我以为我中枪了。”雷克在非洲服事，看到数十万的人得到医治。
blocks.en: In 1908 in Africa, at the first meeting, Lake prayed that the Holy Spirit would be poured out on more than five hundred Zulu people, and revival broke out immediately. While preaching in South Africa, a man disrupted the meeting; Lake pointed at him and said “Sit down,” and the man fell as though struck and lay on the ground for three hours. When he recovered he said, “Something hit me and passed through my body; I thought I had been shot.” Serving in Africa, Lake saw hundreds of thousands of people healed.

blocks.zh: 1912年雷克回到美国，1913年在美国史波肯市建立医治祈祷院。五到六年的时间里，在那里发生了十万件有文献记载的医治个案。根据美国政府当时的统计，“雷克牧师藉着神的医治使史波肯成为全世界最健康的城市”。
blocks.en: Lake returned to the United States in 1912 and in 1913 founded the Healing Prayer Room in Spokane. Within five or six years, a hundred thousand medically documented healing cases occurred there. According to the U.S. government’s statistics at the time, “Pastor Lake, through divine healing, made Spokane the healthiest city in the world.”

blocks.zh: 到1924年，他在全美开拓四十间教会。雷克的事工兴起一位领袖戈登林赛，他创办了“万国基督”，现在分布在一百二十多个国家；另外还有“万国基督学院”，训练了四万多名学生。
blocks.en: By 1924 he had planted forty churches across the nation. Out of Lake’s ministry arose a leader, Gordon Lindsay, who founded “Christ for the Nations,” now present in more than 120 countries; there is also “Christ for the Nations Institute,” which has trained more than forty thousand students.

blocks.zh: 凯尔皮尔斯继承衣钵，继续雷克所开创的医治祈祷院事工。目前有三千多间医治祈祷院，分布在超过七十三个国家。
blocks.en: Kyle Pierce inherited the mantle and continues the healing-prayer-room ministry Lake founded. There are now more than three thousand healing prayer rooms, spread across more than seventy-three countries.

blocks.zh: 有谁规定说，只有特别的人，才能被神复兴，带着大能呢？不是信的人吗？神不偏待人。如果教会历史上，这些复兴是透过这些平凡和普通的人带下，谁规定，你的生命不能被点燃、不能被复兴，不能带着神的大能呢？呼求神吧，神的百姓！用悟性祷告也要用灵祷告，用普通话祷告也要用方言祷告。现在在你内心神同在的那口井里面，透过你的方言祷告按压出生命和能力的活水泉源来吧。
blocks.en: Who has ruled that only special people can be revived by God and carry His power? Is it not those who believe? God does not show favoritism. If, in church history, these revivals were brought through ordinary, common people, who says your life cannot be kindled, cannot be revived, cannot carry the power of God? Cry out to God, people of God! Pray with your understanding and also in the Spirit; pray in your everyday language and also in tongues. Now, from that well of God’s presence within you, press out through your praying in tongues the living spring of life and power.

text.zh:
我得罪了谁？谁又得罪了我？
我又要饶恕谁？
text.en:
Whom have I wronged? Who has wronged me?
Whom do I need to forgive?

title.zh: 救主耶稣也是主、更是君王！
title.en: Jesus Is Our Savior—and He Is Our Lord and King!

verse.zh: 天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了。<small>马太福音 28:18</small>
verse.en: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.<small>Matthew 28:18</small>

verseText.zh: 天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了。
verseText.en: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.

summary.zh: 从“耶稣是救主也是主”讲起：大多数基督徒愿意接受耶稣为救主，却不愿意让耶稣在生命中做主；只有让耶稣做主，耶稣才能成为救主。大使命不只是传福音，更是使人作门徒——传福音、医治病人、教导人跟随耶稣。反思“因信称义”的正确理解——信心必须有因信心生发出来的行为（罗马书4章、6章，彼得后书2章，雅各书2章），立定心志让耶稣作生命的主与君王。附思考问题。
summary.en: Starting from “Jesus is Savior and Lord”: most Christians gladly receive Jesus as Savior, yet are unwilling to let Jesus rule in their lives; only when Jesus is Lord can He become your Savior. The Great Commission is more than evangelism—it is making disciples: preaching the gospel, healing the sick, and teaching people to follow Jesus. It reflects on the correct understanding of “justification by faith”—faith must produce works that spring from faith (Romans 4 and 6, 2 Peter 2, James 2)—and resolves to let Jesus be the Lord and King of life. With reflection questions.

blocks.zh: 大多数基督徒认为耶稣是救主，却不愿意让耶稣做主，而是希望自己做主。
blocks.en: Most Christians believe Jesus is the Savior, yet they are unwilling to let Jesus be Lord—they would rather be lord of their own lives.

blocks.zh: 如果自己仍然在生命的宝座上，你只想要耶稣成为服务你的服务员，你是无法经历耶稣的拯救。
blocks.en: If you are still sitting on the throne of your own life and only want Jesus to be your servant, you will never experience Jesus’ salvation.

blocks.zh: 只有让耶稣做主，耶稣才能成为你的救主。
blocks.en: Only when you let Jesus be Lord can Jesus become your Savior.

blocks.zh: 我们大多数是先接受耶稣成为救主，然后才慢慢在教会生活中学习顺服，让耶稣成为生命的主。在这个过程中，很多人不愿意让耶稣做自己生命的主，就远离了教会。因为他们只想要耶稣做自己的救主，不愿意耶稣在自己的生活中做主。
blocks.en: Most of us first receive Jesus as Savior, then gradually learn submission in church life, letting Jesus become the Lord of our lives. In this process, many people who are unwilling to let Jesus rule their lives drift away from the church—they want Jesus to be their Savior only, not to rule in their daily lives.

blocks.zh: 而耶稣不仅仅要拯救信靠祂的人，更是要我们成为跟随祂的门徒。
blocks.en: Jesus not only wants to save those who trust in Him—He also wants us to become His disciples.

blocks.zh: 教会一直以来把传福音当作教会的大使命。但是耶稣在升天之前说的不仅仅是传福音；综合马可福音和马太福音来看，耶稣说的是传福音，医治病人，教导人跟随耶稣做门徒，遵守耶稣的教导。
blocks.en: The church has long regarded evangelism as the Great Commission. But what Jesus said before His ascension was more than evangelism; looking at both Mark and Matthew together, Jesus spoke of preaching the gospel, healing the sick, and teaching people to follow Him as disciples and obey His teaching.

zh.label: 圣经 · 马太福音 28:18-20
zh.text: 耶稣进前来，对他们说：“天上地下所有的权柄都赐给我了。所以，你们要去，使万民作我的门徒，奉父、子、圣灵的名给他们施洗。凡我所吩咐你们的，都教训他们遵守，我就常与你们同在，直到世界的末了。”

en.label: Bible · Matthew 28:18-20
en.text: Then Jesus came to them and said, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age.”

zh.label: 圣经 · 马可福音 16:15-18
zh.text: 他又对他们说：“你们往普天下去，传福音给万民听。信而受洗的必然得救，不信的必被定罪。信的人必有神迹随着他们，就是：奉我的名赶鬼，说新方言，手能拿蛇；若喝了什么毒物，也必不受害；手按病人，病人就必好了。”

en.label: Bible · Mark 16:15-18
en.text: He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to all creation. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned. And these signs will accompany those who believe: In my name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up snakes with their hands; and when they drink deadly poison, it will not hurt them at all; they will place their hands on sick people, and they will get well.”

blocks.zh: 只有做门徒，才能传福音、医治病人、训练门徒；如果基督徒不愿意付代价跟随耶稣做门徒，就还是停留在基督道理的开端。
blocks.en: Only disciples can preach the gospel, heal the sick, and train disciples. If Christians are unwilling to pay the cost of following Jesus as disciples, they remain at the very beginning of the teachings of Christ.

blocks.zh: 这种不愿意付代价跟随耶稣，和神学历史有一定的关联，因为教会里面教导人的牧者、老师，或多或少都有一些神学背景，甚至有的神学还是互相冲突的。
blocks.en: This unwillingness to pay the cost of following Jesus is connected to the history of theology, because the pastors and teachers who instruct the church all have some theological background, and some theologies even conflict with one another.

blocks.zh: 我认为神学只有回到了圣经，才是好的神学。脱离圣经、超越圣经、否定圣经的神学不是好的神学，也不是正确的神学。
blocks.en: I believe theology is good only when it returns to the Bible. Theology that departs from, goes beyond, or denies the Bible is neither good nor correct.

blocks.zh: 因信称义是新约保罗书信的教导。
blocks.en: Justification by faith is the teaching of Paul’s letters in the New Testament.

blocks.zh: 因信称义的教导来自罗马书，这个观点不是错误的。错误的是人的理解，很多人理解成只要有信心，不需要有行为的改变，这不是保罗的原意。
blocks.en: The teaching of justification by faith comes from Romans, and the view itself is not wrong. What is wrong is people’s understanding—many have come to think that as long as you have faith, no change in behavior is needed. That was never Paul’s intention.

zh.label: 圣经 · 罗马书 4:2-5
zh.text: 倘若亚伯拉罕是因行为称义，就有可夸的，只是在　神面前并无可夸。经上说什么呢？说：“亚伯拉罕信　神，这就算为他的义。”作工的得工价，不算恩典，乃是该得的；惟有不作工的，只信称罪人为义的　神，他的信就算为义。

en.label: Bible · Romans 4:2-5
en.text: If, in fact, Abraham was justified by works, he had something to boast about—but not before God. What does Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” Now to the one who works, wages are not credited as a gift but as an obligation. However, to the one who does not work but trusts God who justifies the ungodly, their faith is credited as righteousness.

zh.label: 圣经 · 罗马书 4:17-22
zh.text: 亚伯拉罕所信的，是那叫死人复活、使无变为有的　神，他在主面前作我们世人的父。如经上所记：“我已经立你作多国的父。”他在无可指望的时候，因信仍有指望，就得以作多国的父，正如先前所说：“你的后裔将要如此。”他将近百岁的时候，虽然想到自己的身体如同已死，撒拉的生育已经断绝，他的信心还是不软弱；并且仰望　神的应许，总没有因不信，心里起疑惑，反倒因信，心里得坚固，将荣耀归给　神。且满心相信　神所应许的必能作成。所以这就算为他的义。

en.label: Bible · Romans 4:17-22
en.text: Abraham, against hope, in hope believed, so that he became the father of many nations, according to what was spoken, “So shall your offspring be.” He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body as good as dead—since he was about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. He did not waver in unbelief at God’s promise but was strengthened in faith and gave glory to God, because he was fully convinced that God was able to do what He had promised. Therefore, it was credited to him as righteousness.

zh.label: 圣经 · 罗马书 9:31-32
zh.text: 但以色列人追求律法的义，反得不着律法的义。这是什么缘故呢？是因为他们不凭着信心求，只凭着行为求，他们正跌在那绊脚石上。

en.label: Bible · Romans 9:31-32
en.text: But the people of Israel, who pursued the law as the way of righteousness, have not attained their goal. Why not? Because they pursued it not by faith but as if it were by works. They stumbled over the stumbling stone.

blocks.zh: 我们看到罗马书六章15节的意思清楚说明，虽然我们因信称义，不在律法之下，乃在恩典之下，但是仍然不可以犯罪！
blocks.en: Romans 6:15 makes it clear that although we are justified by faith and are not under the law but under grace, we still must not sin!

blocks.zh: 彼得说，认识耶稣就脱离了世上的污秽，但如果以后又被世上的罪辖制，末后的光景比之前不信的时候更加不好呢！
blocks.en: Peter says that knowing Jesus delivers us from the corruption of the world—but if we are later enslaved by the sins of the world again, our final condition is worse than when we did not believe!

blocks.zh: 我们看主的兄弟雅各怎么说。
blocks.en: Let us see what James, the Lord’s brother, says.

blocks.zh: 耶稣的兄弟雅各说，信心没有行为是死的，信心要与行为并行，信心才能因为行为得以成全。我们信耶稣之后，就是一个因为信心生发出美好生命的一个过程。不要在过程中灰心，要因为信心而得胜。
blocks.en: James, the brother of Jesus, says that faith without works is dead; faith works together with deeds, and faith is made complete by works. After we believe in Jesus, our lives become a process in which faith brings forth a beautiful life. Do not lose heart in the process—be victorious through faith.

blocks.zh: 平衡整本圣经而不是断章取义才是信仰的根本与核心；基督的信仰需要信心，同时信心也必须有因为信心生发出来的行为。
blocks.en: Balancing the whole Bible rather than taking verses out of context is the root and core of faith. The Christian faith requires faith, and faith must also produce works that spring from faith.

zh.label: 圣经 · 罗马书 6:15
zh.text: 这却怎么样呢？我们在恩典之下，不在律法之下，就可以犯罪吗？断乎不可！

en.label: Bible · Romans 6:15
en.text: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under the law but under grace? By no means!

zh.label: 圣经 · 彼得后书 2:20-22
zh.text: 倘若他们因认识主救主耶稣基督，得以脱离世上的污秽，后来又在其中被缠住、制伏，他们末后的景况就比先前更不好了。他们晓得义路，竟背弃了传给他们的圣命，倒不如不晓得为妙。俗语说得真不错：狗所吐的，它转过来又吃；猪洗净了，又回到泥里去滚。这话在他们身上正合适。

en.label: Bible · 2 Peter 2:20-22
en.text: If they have escaped the corruption of the world by knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and are again entangled in it and are overcome, they are worse off at the end than they were at the beginning. It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then to turn their backs on the sacred command that was passed on to them. Of them the proverbs are true: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and “A sow that is washed returns to her wallowing in the mud.”

zh.label: 圣经 · 雅各书 2:20-22
zh.text: 虚浮的人哪，你愿意知道没有行为的信心是死的吗？我们的祖宗亚伯拉罕把他儿子以撒献在坛上，岂不是因行为称义吗？可见信心是与他的行为并行，而且信心因着行为才得成全。

en.label: Bible · James 2:20-22
en.text: You foolish person, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is useless? Was not our father Abraham considered righteous for what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar? You see that his faith and his actions were working together, and his faith was made complete by what he did.

blocks.zh: 我们信耶稣之后，肯定会有行为不完全，或者自己软弱的地方。但软弱也好、不完全也罢，我们不能以此为借口，只宣称自己的信心，而是从信心开始生发出一个志向：耶稣的十字架已经担当了我的罪，我从此是可以活出不被罪辖制的生命。
blocks.en: After we believe in Jesus, we will certainly have imperfect behavior or places of weakness. But weakness and imperfection cannot be used as an excuse to merely declare our faith. Instead, faith should give birth to a resolution: the cross of Jesus has already carried my sins, and from now on I can live a life that is not enslaved by sin.

blocks.zh: 当我们立定志向跟随耶稣的时候，我相信罪就不能捆绑我们了。如果我们认为我只要信，就是犯罪也没有关系，我们就会在罪中沉沦。
blocks.en: When we set our hearts to follow Jesus, I believe sin can no longer bind us. If we think that as long as we believe, even sinning does not matter, we will sink in sin.

blocks.zh: 我要因信称义得救，也不仅仅因信得救，更是因为信心生发出得救的行为，我们的信才说明我们真的是得救。我们不仅仅要让耶稣成为我们的救主，耶稣更是我们生命的主，我们的君王！阿们！
blocks.en: I am saved by justification through faith—and not only saved by faith, but because faith brings forth saving works, our faith shows that we are truly saved. We must not only let Jesus be our Savior; Jesus is also the Lord of our lives and our King! Amen!

blocks.zh:
你是否愿意让耶稣不只是你的救主，更成为你生命的主？在你生活的哪些领域，你仍然希望自己做主？
你如何理解“因信称义”与“信心生发行为”的关系？信心没有行为是死的吗？
大使命不只是传福音，更是使人作门徒。你愿意付代价跟随耶稣作门徒吗？
blocks.en:
Are you willing to let Jesus be not only your Savior but also the Lord of your life? In which areas of your life do you still want to be in charge yourself?
How do you understand the relationship between “justification by faith” and “faith producing works”? Is faith without works dead?
The Great Commission is not only about preaching the gospel but about making disciples. Are you willing to pay the cost to follow Jesus as a disciple?
